Apple: forecast and valuation dossier

As of 17 October 2026. Latest reported financial period: 27 June 2026; September-quarter actuals are not yet available in the reviewed source set. Dollar amounts below are USD. This is conditional valuation research, not a recommendation to trade.

Bottom line

The evidence supports a durable, modest-growth ecosystem, but does not support extending the latest 16–17% revenue growth or 50.1% gross margin indefinitely. Keep a three-year explicit growth phase before fading to maturity. A base 9%/8%/7% revenue path, first-year 31% operating margin and eventual 32% margin is more informative than immediately fading a single starting rate. Apple's June gross-margin refund benefit and September memory-cost pressure pull near-term margin in opposite directions.

The existing app's 8% growth, 32% target margin, 3x sales/capital, 20% tax and 9% WACC are broadly defensible mature/base judgments. The important changes are timing, margin normalization and the equity bridge. The existing zero additional assets/claims fields are unreviewed placeholders. June noncurrent securities alone are $84.118bn outside snapshot cash. No app changes were made.

Reported operating evidence

Fiscal revenue was $383.285bn in 2023, $391.035bn in 2024 and $416.161bn in 2025. Operating income increased from $114.301bn to $123.216bn to $133.050bn. That is a strong margin record but a much slower revenue record than the latest product cycle. FY2025 operating margin was 31.97%. The last three fiscal quarters produced revenue of $143.756bn, $111.184bn and $109.417bn; trailing-year revenue is $466.823bn and EBIT $154.859bn, a 33.17% margin. Original filing contexts and quarterly calculations are retained in evidence-AAPL.html#facts and evidence-AAPL.html#quarterly-financials. FY2025 annual report, June 2026 10-Q.

June-quarter iPhone revenue was $54.252bn, Mac $10.352bn, iPad $6.191bn, wearablesevidence-AAPL.html#sources $7.883bn and Services $30.739bn. Services supplied 28.1% of revenue and 42.4% of gross profit, with a 75.6% gross margin. It is a material profit engine, but not the whole company. Greater China contributed $18.816bn of quarterly sales; geographic and product concentration remain meaningful. The installed base exceeded 2.5bn active devices in December2025; installed devices are neither unique paying customers nor a disclosed Services monetization denominator. June financial statements, January results.

Reported June gross margin of 50.1% includes approximately two percentage points of tariff refunds. Subtracting that approximate amount gives 48.1% underlying quarterly GM and approximately 32.70% trailing operating margin, not an issuer-reported adjusted measure. The September guide is 47–48% GM including roughly one point of refunds, or 46–47% underlying. Higher memory costs and exhaustion of favorable inventory costs explain the prospective compression. A services-mix benefit cannot simply cancel an unmodeled hardware-cost shock. July release, July management call transcript, secondary host.

Management outlook and its track record

July30 outlook for September: total revenue growth 9–11%, iPhone mid-teens, Services near the June growth pace allowing for FX, operating expense $19.1–19.4bn and tax about16.5%. FX was expected to worsen sequentially by about2.5 percentage points, and supply constraints to increase. This is one-quarter conditional outlook, not a formal annual or multiyear CAGR commitment. No December-quarter actual or management forecast is invented.

The 12-quarter history, FY2023Q4–FY2026Q3, preserves original dated outlooks and matching original financial periods. Numeric gross-margin outcomes: seven within, five above, zero below; mean reported midpoint error +0.56 percentage points. June2026's reported beat largely disappears after the approximate refund adjustment. Only the latest three completed quarters have explicit numeric revenue-growth ranges in this sample: actual growth 15.65% versus10–12%, 16.60% versus13–16%, and16.36% versus14–17%. Earlier descriptions such as low-to-mid-single digits are not assigned invented endpoints. The March2024 outlook also excluded roughly$5bn of prior-year catch-up sales from its comparison; it must not be scored against an unadjusted flat-revenue forecast.

Readable issuer-hosted historical transcripts were not verified. Quartr transcripts on Stock Analysis supply management wording; SEC filings and issuer releases supply actuals. This weakens confidence in nuances, and is explicitly recorded rather than presenting secondary material as issuer-hosted. Historical webcast replays were advertised for approximately two weeks. Detailed errors, definitions and gaps are in evidence-AAPL.html#guidance. No numerical management-credibility adjustment is applied.

Good reported outcomes do not mean accurate demand planning. In July, management acknowledged underestimating iPhone/Mac demand and resulting supply limits. April30 also retired the formal net-cash-neutral target; future buybacks should not be forced to follow an obsolete cash objective. April call.

Reinvestment, cash conversion and dilution

Trailing CFO was $146.724bn and cash capex $10.041bn. Their difference, $136.683bn, is not unlevered owner cash flow: CFO includes SBC addbacks and volatile working capital. R&D reached $42.901bn TTM and SBC $13.706bn. If R&D is capitalized analytically, both NOPAT and invested capital must be restated; do not add an asset without changing earnings/reinvestment.

Nine-month cash capex $6.799bn was below D&A $9.973bn, but that does not imply zero economic reinvestment. Inventory rose from $5.718bn to $11.092bn; its cash-flow effect was -$5.461bn. Other assets used $16.266bn and payables $5.203bn, partly offset by receivable collections and other liabilities. The final $8.8bn deemed-repatriation tax payment is a separate nonrecurring cash-tax item. Outsourced manufacturing leaves Apple with $57bn of manufacturing purchase obligations, $56.2bn due within a year, plus other purchase obligations. Do not add overlapping obligation schedules or treat all supplier purchases as financing debt. 10-Q cash flow, notes and MD&A.

A 2.5–3x early incremental sales/capital ratio is a judgment that charges for inventory, ecosystem investment and supplier dependence despite low owned capex. Buybacks and expensed intangibles inflate book ROIC; they do not establish an infinite return on incremental economic capital. Base terminal ROIC is20%, falling to13% in the downside case.

Cash repurchases were $62.094bn over nine months, versus roughly$61.8bn program transaction cost; timing and definitions differ. Dividends used $11.778bn and equity-award tax withholding $6.462bn. Unrecognized compensation was $26.7bn over about2.7years. Retain SBC as an economic expense and reconcile future awards/shares or replacement repurchases; do not add back SBC and also assume dilution-free cash distributions.

Leadership evidence

John Ternus became CEO on September1,2026, with Tim Cook becoming executive chairman. The completed financial/forecast sample is a Cook-era record, spanning CFO Maestri and Parekh. Ternus's prior hardware leadership is relevant but is not a multiyear CEO track record. Issuer succession announcement.

Ternus's October TIME interview emphasizes integrated devices, software and personal context, while acknowledging memory constraints. The thesis is useful; it does not prove AI monetization. Apple confirmed Duo preorders beginning October16 and describes Siri AI as an English-language beta rollout. New-product revenue, contribution margin and retention have not been reported. evidence-AAPL.html#management distinguishes demonstrated demand, delivery, cost control and cash returns from these unproven outcomes. Direct TIME interview, issuer product update.

Conditional forecast proposals

All rates below are analyst judgments. Annual periods run from the latest June trailing-year anchor; Apple's first modeled year is not identical to its September fiscal year. Growth fades linearly after the early phase. Capital efficiency fades over the last five years to match terminal ROIC, avoiding free terminal growth.

Base early margins are31%/31.5%/32%; base early incremental sales/capital2.5x/2.5x/3x. The bull requires persistent premium upgrades and Services profit expansion, reaching$1.287tn sales at maturity. That is a conditional scale claim, not a market-size estimate. The bear allows low growth and27.5% mature EBIT margin. Enterprise-to-common-equity bridge and decision gates

June cash/equivalents $39.544bn plus current securities$22.855bn equals app snapshot cash$62.399bn. Noncurrent securities$84.118bn are not included there. Review availability and operating cash needs, then count them once. Exact debt components are current term$11.007bn plus noncurrent$71.340bn plus CP$1.997bn = $84.344bn. The note's rounded82.3bn term-debt figure is not the exact balance-sheet sum.

Cover shares are14.59418bn as of July17 versus14.608963bn at June27; weighted diluted historical shares are a different concept. Complete lease tables are last available in the reviewed FY2025 annual report: finance$1.230bn and operating$12.490bn. They must not be mislabeled June balances. A conditional Amazon/Globalstar transaction also contemplates redemption of Apple's interests in a special-purpose entity; no proceeds amount is assumed and no value is added before reconciliation. See evidence-AAPL.html#sources for the counterparty filing.

Do not publish a per-share value until leases, investments, taxes and outstanding awards are reconciled with forecast cash flows. Regulatory/distribution/search-economics changes, China competition, component supply, inventory mismatch and AI development/serving costs are core invalidators. Watch underlying GM after refunds, Services growth, inventory-to-sales, supply recovery and cash conversion. A credible review would revise the scenario inputs, not attach a generic management discount.

Files and limitations

evidence-AAPL.html#facts retains original financial evidence; evidence-AAPL.html#sources dates and scopes sources; evidence-AAPL.html#guidance preserves the12-quarter comparisons; evidence-AAPL.html#judgment supplies annual schedules and mathematical scale checks; evidence-AAPL.html#management separates capabilities and tenure. Remaining gaps are current complete lease balances, a fully cleared common-equity bridge, product-level AI returns and readable primary Apple historical transcripts. No complete search of every interview or intraperiod revision is claimed.

Microsoft: forecast and valuation dossier

As of 17 October 2026. Latest reported financial period: 30 June 2026. September2026/FY2027Q1 actuals are not assumed. All dollar amounts are USD. Conditional valuation research, not a trading recommendation.

Bottom line

Microsoft's demand and distribution evidence supports a longer growth phase than a mature software-only model, but the capital burden has changed fundamentally. Use five explicit early years in the base and bull cases, then a fade to maturity. Base revenue growth18%/17%/15%/13%/11% reaches approximately$661bn in year5 and$1.217tn in year15. That requires successful monetization and utilization, not simply a large order book.

The largest modeling trap is treating the revised $175bn CY2026 capex outlook as an economic cut from$190bn. From FY2027 Microsoft extends datacenter/office building lives from15 to25years. More future datacenter leases then classify as operating rather than finance, removing them from reported capex. Management says underlying investment intentions are unchanged; the near-term depreciation benefit is expected to be small. A cash-flow model must follow economic investment and lease payments through the reclassification. Official July call.

Existing base assumptions of18% growth,42% mature margin,0.6x sales/capital,22% tax and9.5% WACC are not irrational, but a single constant capital ratio misses the investment surge. Proposed base uses front-loaded0.45x/0.50x/0.60x/0.70x/0.80x marginal sales/capital, eventually43% EBIT margin and15-year maturity. No app edits were made.

Reported growth, mix and profit evidence

Revenue advanced from$245.122bn in FY2024 to$281.724bn in FY2025 and$331.839bn in FY2026. EBIT rose$109.433bn/$128.528bn/$155.237bn; operating margins44.64%/45.62%/46.78%. FY2026 revenue grew17.8%, EBIT20.8%. These figures support genuine operating leverage, but not a conclusion that AI infrastructure has software-like marginal capital needs. FY2026 annual report.

FY2026 Microsoft Cloud revenue was approximately$214.4bn,+27%; Azure exceeded$100bn,+41%. In Q4, consolidated revenue was$90.007bn. Approximate segment revenues were PBP$37.8bn, Intelligent Cloud$39.3bn and More Personal Computing$12.9bn, with respective margins58%,41% and21%. PBP's productivity economics help finance lower-margin infrastructure. Consumer/gaming weakness and impairments are counterexamples to a uniformly successful portfolio. More than30m paid M365Copilot seats and consumption pricing demonstrate adoption, but do not disclose product contribution profit or incremental price per retained seat. Issuer call and Q&A.

Commercial RPO reached$678bn,+84%, versus25% growth excluding OpenAI; average duration2.3years, about30% expected to convert over the next12months. Treat duration, conversion and credit exposure separately. Related-party OpenAI commercial revenue, including revenue-sharing payments, was$24.1bn, about7.3% of company sales; accounts receivable were$6.0bn. That is distinct from Microsoft's approximately25% equity stake, $13bn funding commitment ($11.9bn funded), and nonoperating investment gains. A large contract backed by a customer raising capital is not equivalent to cash already earned. Annual report, investment and revenue notes.

Guidance quality, revisions and comparability

The primary issuer hosts readable full transcripts. The12-quarter sample FY2024Q1–FY2026Q4 matches original next-quarter guidance to the same nominal revenue periods. All12 results exceeded the original upper bound; mean midpoint error+2.44%, median+2.16%. Earlier consolidated ranges are explicitly derived sums of the three segment ranges. A one-quarter beat does not establish an unbiased forecast or justify increasing every modeled growth rate.

Azure's metric definition changed for FY2025. The original July2024 guide of28–29% CC growth is not comparable with34% reported under the revised definition. The August21 mechanical reissue guided approximately33% under the new definition, followed by34% actual. EMS/per-user PowerBI and other reporting changes shifted category boundaries; consolidated revenue outlook remained unchanged. FY2024 results used in the history retain the contemporaneous basis. Original reporting-change exhibit.

Longer capacity forecasts have required revision. January2025 expected AI supply roughly balanced with near-term demand by FY2025 end; April pushed constraints beyond June; October2025 extended them at least through FY2026; April2026 at least through calendar2026. Demand growth and capacity delivery both matter, so these revisions are evidence of timing uncertainty, not proof of deployment failure alone.

FY2026 operating margin was initially expected slightly lower. January2026 revised to slightly higher, April to roughly one point higher including expected retirement-program expense; actual was+1.16points. This matched the last approximate view more closely than the initial view. The full history preserves original versus revised versions instead of silently replacing a forecast.

Current FY2027Q1 outlook: revenue$89.85–90.95bn, Azure approximately45% CC growth, COGS$29.6–29.8bn, opex$16.8–16.9bn, tax about20%, capex more than$50bn. FY2027 revenue and EBIT should grow double digits, operating margin decline less than1point, opex rise mid/high single digits, capex grow and cash FCF remain positive. These are pending conditional forecasts. There is no verified formal multiyear revenue CAGR commitment. Official July outlook, detailed dates/errors in evidence-MSFT.html#guidance.

Capital intensity, accounting and cash conversion

Cash PP&E spend accelerated$44.477bn/$64.551bn/$115.948bn across FY2024–2026, while finance-lease right-of-use additions reached$24.608bn in FY2026. Cash capex plus those additions totals$140.556bn. A reported capex metric can differ because of delivery and recognition timing; it is not automatically identical to annual cash-flow capex plus every lease addition.

The annual report's $34.3bn is depreciation alone. Cash-flow “depreciation, amortization and other” is$38.534bn, and intangible amortization is separately about$4.7bn. Do not relabel the depreciation-only line full D&A, or assume the CFO reconciliation line is a clean D&A subtotal. Cash capex plus finance-lease additions minus that reconciliation addback is about$102.0bn against$50.1bn incremental revenue, a rough0.49x sales/investment proxy before working capital and other adjustments. This is a useful warning, not a fully normalized return calculation. Annual financial statements and notes8/10/13.

CFO was$182.935bn and cashcapex FCF$66.987bn. CFO includes$12.405bn SBC addback and timing effects: receivables used$12.737bn, while payables added$5.268bn and unearned revenue$9.361bn. Other investing outflows increased substantially from component facilitation. Cash FCF excludes newly incurred finance-lease investment and finance principal paid in financing; a valuation must reconcile that rather than assuming it is all distributable owner cash.

At June30, finance-lease liabilities were$66.594bn and operating$21.925bn. Additional uncommenced leases were$329.1bn, starting FY2027–2033 with1–20year terms. The contractual lease total$443.506bn includes undiscounted payments, interest and uncommenced arrangements; it is not an extra debt balance to subtract in full. Purchase commitments$194.060bn and construction$34.566bn further constrain flexibility. Count future investment/rent and financing consistently, avoiding both omission and double counting.

Longer building accounting lives do not change server/accelerator replacement cash needs. Q4 capex was predominantly shorter-lived CPU/GPU equipment. Stress faster obsolescence, component inflation, power delays and excess capacity after current shortages ease. Conversely, lower unit costs and better utilization can improve returns, but demand may also consume those savings through pricing and heavier usage.

Management capability and interview evidence

Nadella has been CEO since February2014 and Hood CFO since May2013, spanning the measured period. The evidence shows sustained commercial growth and cost discipline, not proof of individual causality. Product adoption and reported datacenter deployment improvements support execution; shifting capacity dates, consumer weakness and huge uncommenced commitments are material counterexamples. evidence-MSFT.html#management evaluates five dimensions and identifies these limits.

In the March4 Morgan Stanley interview, Nadella described returns as a function of utilization across hardware generations, diverse customers and applications, plus subscription and metered consumption economics. This explains why Azure growth alone cannot capture all investment benefits, but is not a numerical project-ROI guarantee. Primary conference transcript.

Conditional forecast proposals

Annual year1 is FY2027. After the stated early phase, growth fades linearly to terminal growth; capital efficiency converges to the value consistent with mature margin, tax and terminal ROIC during the final five years.

CaseEarly annual revenue growthEarly years / maturityMature EBIT marginTaxWACCTerminal growth / ROICMaturity sales

bull22%, 22%, 20%, 18%, 16%5 / 2046%20%9%3% / 22%$2,956.0bn
bear12%, 10%, 8%3 / 1036%23%10.5%2% / 11%$603.2bn

The base begins at46% operating margin, consistent with management's less-than1point decline from46.78%, then gradually fades to43%. Front-loaded investment leaves little first-year simplified FCFF despite strong operating profit. All three scenarios remain positive-FCFF in this particular arithmetic; that is not a guarantee. More severe supply costs, lease commitments or an unfavorable working-capital swing can make cash flow negative.

The bull's $2.956tn maturity revenue and$1.360tn operating profit are especially demanding: almost9x current sales over20years. It requires major expansion of global enterprise spending and a durable Microsoft share of AI/application value. It is not validated by a20-year horizon alone. The bear still reaches$603bn sales; it is a slower-growth/margin-pressure case, not a catastrophic scenario. Independent recession, major security, customer-credit and regulatory shocks remain outside that range.

Base terminal marginalROIC16% exceeds9.5% WACC but is below the near-term software franchise's accounting returns. Bull22% and bear11% test persistence of excess returns. Base22% normalized operating tax is above recent quarterly20% outlook and excludes investment gains from operating logic. WACC uses Treasury5.09% observed October16, chosen ERP4.5%, assumed beta1.05 and5% debt weight; the build rounds9.55% to9.5%. No beta regression, market-value capital structure or current bond spread was independently estimated.

Claims, investments, financing and dilution gates

Cash plus short-term investments$76.843bn is already in the snapshot. Long-term investments$36.348bn are separate carrying values, not guaranteed cash realizations. Remove investment gains from operating forecasts; if an investment is added separately, do not also capitalize the same underlying investment distributions in operating value. Operating customer revenue from OpenAI is a separate commercial stream with its own costs and credit risk.

Financial debt carrying amount$40.294bn excludes leases; contractual face principal$46.136bn is a different measurement. The IRS continues to propose$28.9bn additional tax plus penalties/interest on transfer-pricing issues. Microsoft disputes this and believes reserves adequate. Neither subtracting the entire demand as certain incremental debt nor assuming zero exposure is justified; reconcile reserves and stress incremental outcomes.

FY2026 program buybacks cost$16.719bn for about36m shares. The cash-flow repurchase line$22.271bn includes employee-tax withholding; dividend cash was$26.445bn versus$27.035bn declared. Share count stayed near7.43bn, so an automatic large future shrink is unsupported. SBC$12.405bn remains a cost; unrecognized stock-award compensation$24.8bn over about3years and292m shares authorized for future grants are not the same as currently outstanding dilution.

Cover shares7.425545bn, period-end7.427bn and historical weighted diluted7.453bn serve different purposes. A per-share value remains gated until lease-consistent cash flow, nonoperating investments, contingencies and awards are reconciled. evidence-MSFT.html#judgment includes operating-EV illustrations solely as mathematical consequences, with per-share values null.

What would change the thesis

Track Azure growth against delivered capacity; RPO conversion and customer concentration; cloud gross margins; cash/lease/prepayment investment together; Copilot monetization versus usage cost; and impairment/replacement experience. Growth slowing as capacity becomes available would be more damaging than growth limited by documented shortages. A falling reported capex figure with rising lease cash payments is not an efficiency win. Higher economic depreciation, pricing competition, security/reliability failures and tax/regulatory exposure can invalidate the scenario even while headline bookings remain high.

Amazon forecast and valuation dossier

Research cutoff: October 17, 2026. Latest reported quarter: June 30, 2026, released July 30; 10-Q filed July 31. USD billions unless stated. This is an analytical scenario proposal, not investment advice, issuer guidance or analyst consensus. No Q3 actuals were available by the cutoff. Financial history contains 14 quarters and FY2023–FY2025. All videos are not watched; readable transcript coverage is specified below.

Decision-useful conclusion

AWS acceleration warrants an explicit three-year high-growth phase rather than fading growth immediately. It does not warrant valuing AI capacity as capital-light software. A proposed base is 18%, 17%, 15% revenue growth for years 1–3, then a fade to 2.5% by year 15, a 16% mature operating margin, 24% normalized tax, 10.25% WACC, and 12% terminal ROIC. Early sales/incremental-capital ratios of 0.65, 0.75 and 0.85 keep substantial build-out costs in the forecast.

These are conditional research inputs. Do not install them as production defaults while the model omits the investment, customer-financing, lease and acquisition bridge. Existing zero nonoperating-asset/claim placeholders are materially incomplete. The proposed path reaches $1.232tn revenue in year 3 and $3.160tn in year 15, with $506bn mature EBIT. That is a demanding scale claim, not merely a small adjustment to near-term growth.

1. What actually changed

The latest quarter delivered revenue $200.606bn, +19.6%, and EBIT $27.461bn, a 13.69% margin. Q1 revenue was $181.519bn, versus $155.667bn a year earlier. AWS accelerated from 17.5% in Q2 2025 to about 20% in Q3, 24% in Q4, 28% in Q1 2026 and 36.7% in Q2 2026. This supports a genuine operating inflection, although quarter-to-quarter growth contains capacity timing and Prime Day distortions. Q2 2026 filing

AWS generates approximately 60.5% of reported segment/consolidated EBIT from 21.1% of sales. Product mix is online stores $70.432bn, physical stores $5.794bn, third-party seller services $46.780bn, advertising $19.809bn, subscriptions $13.730bn, AWS $42.232bn and other $1.829bn. These product categories overlap the geographic segments; do not add advertising on top of segment revenue. AI and chip run-rates above $25bn each also overlap and are not separately additive segments. Q2 release

Annual revenue rose from $574.785bn in 2023 to $637.959bn in 2024 and $716.924bn in 2025. FY2025 AWS sales were $128.725bn and EBIT $45.606bn. North America EBIT was $29.619bn; International $4.750bn. TTM June revenue is $775.680bn, EBIT $93.712bn, margin 12.08%. The machine-readable file preserves source observations and derived quarterly cash-flow figures. FY2025 filing

2. Management outlook, revisions and interviews

Formal guidance

The July 30 outlook for Q3 was $197–202bn revenue and $22.5–26.5bn operating income. Moving Prime Day from Q3 into Q2 lowers the reported Q3 growth comparison by nearly four percentage points; FX was expected to subtract approximately 80bp. The guide excludes energy-derivative remeasurement and assumes no additional acquisitions, restructurings or legal settlements. The Q3 outcome remains open at this cutoff. Issuer guidance

The original February 5 FY2026 capex outlook was approximately $200bn. July 30 call commentary raised cash capex to approximately $220bn, citing memory costs. Consequently, a 10% spending increase cannot be treated as a 10% capacity increase. Original outlook, readable July call

Readable management evidence
  • April 9, 2026 shareholder letter: Jassy says AWS added 3.9GW in 2025 and targets doubling total power capacity by end-2027. Capex precedes customer billing by roughly 6–24 months. The letter distinguishes long-lived buildings from shorter-lived chips/servers, reports customer commitments against much of the build, and describes Trainium3 shipping and Trainium4's approximate future availability. These are management operational claims and targets, not audited incremental ROIC. Letter
  • July 30 earnings call: selected prepared remarks and Q&A were read in a public third-party transcription. Management describes server payback below three years, persistent capacity shortages into 2027, and an undated possibility of AWS becoming a $1tn revenue business. The last item is an aspiration with no forecast horizon, not a base-case target. The transcription is not issuer-certified. Transcript
  • October 8, 2026 a16z interview with AWS CEO Matt Garman: original publisher/video metadata were checked; the public automated transcript was read, particularly approximately 00:16–00:25. Garman discusses power, chips, memory and construction bottlenecks, reserving capacity for smaller customers, and enterprise production adoption. He frames demand as durable but provides no formal multi-year AWS growth rate. Claims about customer ROI and concentration are executive observations, not independently audited findings. Recording date was not disclosed. Original publisher, text read
  • June 23, 2026 Platformer interview: original public page and Amazon's excerpt were read. Garman's survey of CIOs combines positive ROI already achieved with a prospective path to ROI. It cannot establish that 90% of all enterprises currently earn positive AI returns. The issuer excerpt has no visible exact publication date, so none is invented. Original interview, issuer excerpt
Forecasting track record

The separate scorecard covers 12 consecutive target quarters, Q3 2023 through Q2 2026, using each original preceding-quarter issuer range, not a selection of recent beats. Revenue was above range in 9, within in 3, below in 0. EBIT was above in 10, within in 2, below in 0. Every entry stores dates, actual-period sources, midpoint error and distance outside the range.

This is evidence of conservative ranges plus delivery, not proof that management forecasts exact demand or future AI returns. Q3 2025 GAAP EBIT was within range but contained approximately $4.3bn of new settlement/severance charges that the original guide excluded; issuer commentary excluding these put EBIT above range. Q2 2026 includes $640m tariff refunds and $551m energy-derivative gains. Subtracting both still leaves $26.270bn, above the $24bn high, but that sensitivity is not a substitute for the reported outcome. Annual capex vintages and the undated $1tn aspiration are deliberately scored separately.

3. Economics that the valuation must retain

Cash and physical capital. TTM operating cash flow was $161.403bn. Gross cash PPE purchases were $173.028bn; proceeds/incentives $4.021bn; net cash capex $169.007bn. Issuer FCF was therefore negative $7.604bn, not OCF minus gross capex. TTM physical depreciation was $49.741bn, while cash-flow D&A was $75.200bn and includes other amortization. Treating all D&A as physical replacement capex would overstate sustainable cash generation. H1 net cash capex was $96.3bn. Q2 filing

Asset lives and margins. In 2025 Amazon shortened the useful life of a subset of servers from six to five years, after extending server lives from five to six years in 2024. The 2025 change increased depreciation approximately $1.4bn. Longer-lived heavy equipment moved in the opposite direction. These estimates affect accounting margins but do not erase replacement spending. Q2 energy marks predominantly benefited AWS and can reverse. The base 16% mature consolidated margin rests on AWS/advertising mix and fulfillment efficiency, not indefinitely retaining today's 39% AWS segment margin.

Working capital and tax. Retail supplier financing and fast cash collection help fund operations, but seasonal payable swings are not perpetual free financing. Model inventories, receivables, payables and customer payments together. Accelerated tax depreciation/R&D deductions affect cash timing; normalized 24% tax is an inference, not the investment-gain-distorted recent effective tax rate. A separate deferred-tax schedule is preferable.

SBC and dilution. TTM SBC was $19.314bn. June common shares were 10,783m versus 10,731m at December, and H1 diluted weighted-average shares were 10,889m. Keep SBC in operating margins; do not add it back to FCFF while also assuming zero employee dilution. The unrecognized compensation backlog is not identical to a current cash liability.

ROIC. AWS profit growth provides evidence of monetization, but no audited incremental AI-vintage ROIC is disclosed. Consolidated equity is inflated by unrealized AI-investment marks, and lease treatment changes invested capital. This dossier therefore does not present a spurious historical ROIC precise to a decimal. The proposed 12% terminal ROIC is a transparent inference; its reinvestment identity is enforced in the scenario file.

4. Financing, assets and unresolved claims

June cash plus marketable securities totaled $122.988bn; debt carrying value $132.224bn; finance leases $13.451bn; operating leases $96.320bn. Uncommenced leases of $137.214bn and unconditional purchase obligations of $130.065bn are undiscounted future commitments, not automatically incremental net debt if cash-flow forecasts already include their assets/costs.

The investment bridge is substantial: Anthropic preferred carrying value $92.5bn, Anthropic convertible notes fair value $97.9bn, and OpenAI preferred $28.7bn at June. Another $21.3bn was invested in OpenAI after June, disclosed before filing. That event requires a matching cash reduction when adding investment assets. An Anthropic facility had $15bn remaining, with availability linked to compute-delivery milestones. Private-asset marks, customer funding, cloud commitments and future revenue are economically related; do not add each without considering dependencies, taxes, credit risk and liquidity restrictions.

AWS backlog was approximately $496bn, weighted-average remaining contract life 6.4 years. Recognition depends on usage and performance; backlog is neither immediate cash nor an independent asset to add to enterprise value.

The April 13 Globalstar agreement implied approximately $10.9bn enterprise value including debt, with cash/stock elections, cash capped at 40% of shares, milestone adjustments and expected 2027 closing conditions. Separate Apple agreements include services and redemption of interests in a Globalstar entity. Acquisition cash, dilution and assets require a conditional transaction schedule. Do not simply subtract $10.9bn as current debt.

The proposal contains an itemized obligation/asset register with source, date, conditionality and proposed treatment. None of these uncertainties is silently assumed to be zero. Q2 notes 2–4 and commitments

No scenario probabilities or price target were fitted. The cost-of-capital framework uses verified October 16 Treasury 10-year 5.09%; the 4.5% ERP, beta and financing weights are chosen assumptions, not measured October forward returns.

Monitor: AWS growth and backlog conversion against actual capacity delivery; customer financing quality; capex/revenue and physical depreciation; normalized retail margin; AI pricing and server useful life; energy/power costs; net dilution and debt funding. Two ordinary quarters below 20% AWS growth despite new capacity, or continued extraordinary capex with little 2027–2028 operating-cash conversion, would materially weaken the proposed base.

No analyst-consensus estimates are used. Older annual capex revision history was not exhaustively reconstructed. No video viewing is claimed, no paid access was bypassed, and no full commercial transcript is stored.

Alphabet forecast and valuation dossier

Research cutoff: October 17, 2026. Latest reported quarter: June 30, released July 22; 10-Q filed July 23. USD billions unless stated. This dossier concerns Alphabet's common equity economic business, using GOOG as the research ticker; class-specific preferred conversion remains separate. Proposals are analytical inference, not issuer forecasts, consensus or price calibration. No Q3 2026 actuals are included.

Decision-useful conclusion

Cloud acceleration and TPU hardware deliveries justify a three-year explicit growth phase, but the business is becoming more capital-intensive and financially complex. Proposed base revenue growth is 22%, 20%, 18% in years 1–3, fading to 2.5% by year 15, with 32% mature operating margin, 22% normalized tax, 10% WACC and 16% terminal ROIC. Early sales/incremental-capital ratios are 0.50, 0.55 and 0.60, capturing capex and inventory pressure.

This path reaches $770bn revenue in year 3 and $2.292tn by year 15, with $733bn mature EBIT. That scale requires sustained global Search/AI monetization and a much larger Cloud market; it is not established by today's backlog. Maintain the preferred/asset/financing review gate. No observed GOOG price was used to choose growth, margins, duration, capital efficiency or discount rates.

1. Latest operating evidence and historical context

Q2 revenue was $119.796bn, +24.2%, operating income $40.770bn, and operating margin 34.03%. Q1 revenue was $109.896bn, +21.8%; operating income $39.696bn. Net income is unsuitable for extrapolation: Q2 other income/expense was approximately $97.983bn, primarily unrealized investment gains. TTM revenue is $445.866bn, EBIT $147.628bn, margin 33.11%. The April call explicitly attributes the $5bn range increase to Intersect, completed in March; it also anticipates a significant increase in 2027. July raises the range another $15bn at its midpoint for capacity acceleration, again expects significant 2027 growth, and warns of depreciation, energy and other infrastructure expenses. Q3 use of third-party capacity is expected to put modest pressure on Cloud margins. April 29 issuer transcript, July 22 issuer transcript

Product and demand commentary

July management commentary says TPU system deliveries to customer data centers started in Q2, with a relatively small portion of existing-agreement revenue recognized in 2026 and the vast majority in 2027. These shipments can make revenue lumpy. Management also flags tougher Search comparisons and near-term FX effects. No numerical total-revenue or operating-income quarterly range is provided. July call

September 8, 2026: Thomas Kurian at Goldman Sachs Communacopia. The issuer-hosted preliminary transcript was read; no video was watched. Kurian describes large-deal/customer growth and three TPU routes: cloud consumption, systems sold for customer facilities, and infrastructure-provider partnerships. Hardware sales can move facility/power investment to customers, but introduce inventory, delivery and contract-mix risks. He describes broad AI adoption and estimates better customer lifetime economics; these are management cohort estimates, not audited realized ROI. A moderator's promotional market-leadership characterization is not treated as market-share evidence. Issuer-hosted interview

Issuer calls from Q4 2023 through Q2 2026 were reviewed for outlook, capex and relevant business commentary. The source ledger identifies exact event dates and text coverage. Their transcripts are readable issuer material; no investor-day revenue target was substituted where none was found.

Guidance track record: do not manufacture a hit rate

The record contains 11 consecutive earnings communications. Alphabet did not provide numerical next-quarter total-revenue or EBIT ranges in these reviewed calls. That absence is recorded as not provided, never zero. It would be misleading to construct a CEO revenue accuracy score from sell-side estimates or reported growth.

Quantified capex observations are scored with their original semantics: approximately $12bn-or-more quarterly levels in 2024 are floors, not narrow ranges; approximately $13bn for Q4 2024 is a point with no invented tolerance; the Q1 2025 $16–18bn range contains actual capex. Directional FY2024 operating-margin expansion was delivered. The exit-2024 YouTube-plus-Cloud run-rate target exceeded $100bn and management subsequently reported $110bn; that combined measure includes YouTube subscriptions and must not be checked against YouTube advertising alone. 2024 Q1 outlook, 2024 Q3 outlook, 2024 Q4 results/outlook

3. Capital, cash conversion and operating quality

Capacity and depreciation. H1 capex was $80.598bn, including Q2 $44.924bn; H1 physical depreciation was $13.586bn. TTM capex $132.402bn exceeds TTM depreciation $25.237bn by over $107bn before working capital, leases and acquisitions. June net PPE was $321.212bn. A one-parameter sales/capital model must not confuse depreciation lag with permanently high free cash generation.

Working capital. H1 inventory absorbed $7.739bn cash, receivables $6.904bn and other assets $9.950bn, partially offset by payables, accrued liabilities, customer liabilities and taxes. TPU systems are not just a renamed subscription business: control-transfer hardware recognition, returns, installation/support obligations and inventory economics matter. H1 OCF was $84.859bn and FCF $4.261bn. Q2 OCF $39.069bn minus capex $44.924bn produced negative $5.855bn FCF. Q2 cash flows and revenue policy

Acquisitions. Wiz closed March 11 for about $29.5bn after adjustments, excluding post-combination compensation; Intersect closed March 10 for about $5.9bn. These are not entirely organic growth or ordinary PPE purchases. Wiz creates amortization/compensation effects, and Intersect adds capacity and energy development. Model acquisition investment separately from the compressed organic sales/capital proxy.

SBC and share count. H1 cash-flow SBC add-back was $14.708bn, while the allocated expense disclosure rounds to $15.2bn. Do not equate the two definitions. TTM cash-flow SBC was $28.147bn. Common shares were 12,230m at June versus 12,088m at December; H1 diluted weighted average 12,274m. There were no H1 common repurchases. Do not automatically carry historical buyback-driven per-share accretion into this financing regime.

Margins, tax and ROIC. The proposed mature 32% margin is below current TTM 33.11%, allowing for AI compute, energy, hardware mix and central research. A normalized 22% tax rate is an inference; huge investment marks and deferred tax changes distort current effective rates. The terminal 16% ROIC assumes durable intellectual-property/distribution advantages but meaningful physical capital. No audited marginal return for the latest AI build is available, and segment EBIT omits shared costs. Therefore, a precise historical incremental AI ROIC is not claimed.

4. Backlog, financing and unresolved common-share claims

June total backlog was $519.5bn, including $513.9bn Cloud. Management expects just over 50% to be recognized over the next 24 months. Timing depends on duration, delivery and utilization; amounts include deferred revenue and future invoices, exclude cancellable contracts and include TPU hardware arrangements. This supports visibility but is not a guaranteed annualized service run-rate or an asset to add separately to enterprise value.

June cash/current marketables totaled $242.474bn, but included $87.063bn marketable equity, of which $80bn was restricted SpaceX. Additional noncurrent investments totaled $145.587bn. These are valuation-sensitive investments, not interchangeable operating cash; current equity must not be added a second time. Debt carrying value was $100.164bn; finance leases $2.590bn; operating leases $18.037bn. Uncommenced leases were $85.2bn undiscounted; another $5.8bn short-term capacity commitment starts in Q3.

The financing structure changed materially. Common and mandatory-convertible preferred capital were raised in H1. Preferred legal liquidation preference is $19.25bn, while the balance-sheet book amount is $18.023bn after issuance/capped-call effects. The 6.25% preferred converts using class-specific future VWAP formulas, with ordinary gross common dilution approximately 43.56–54.46m shares, before dividend/adjustment effects. A $40bn ATM authorization was unsold at June. The existing detailed preferred review must be retained; do not combine a full preferred-principal deduction with full conversion dilution. Do not assume book value equals fair value or claim capped calls remove every dilution outcome.

Data-center credit backstops had $43.785bn notional maximum exposure, energy-infrastructure guarantees approximately $7.6bn maximum potential payments, and contingent strategic funding equity derivatives $20bn notional. The amounts are not expected losses or automatically current debt: default triggers, lease takeover/sublease rights, termination rights, timing and recorded derivative liabilities matter. They are also not zero-risk footnotes. August debt issuance requires a matched cash/proceeds/uses bridge if moving beyond the June anchor. Q2 notes on investments, derivatives, leases, debt and equity

The base first-year growth cross-check uses roughly 60% Cloud growth on a 17.4% TTM revenue weight and 14% elsewhere, producing about 22%. This is an inference from demand/capacity evidence, not a company forecast. The mature sales/capital ratio is linked algebraically to terminal ROIC and after-tax margin, rather than independently selecting incompatible favorable assumptions.

The bull stress reaches $6.900tn revenue and $2.484tn EBIT, a very demanding 15.5-times scale expansion. It is an upper-bound duration/market-expansion stress, not a central planning case. The bear reaches $738bn revenue. No probability weights are assigned. WACC uses the common verified October 16 Treasury input of 5.09%, with a chosen 4.5% ERP and assumed beta/financing mix; these latter inputs are not observed forward returns.

Weaken the base if Search growth drops below mid-single digits while compute/TAC rises; backlog conversion materially misses management's 24-month timing; TPU hardware carries inferior margins or inventory risks; 2027 capex grows without cash conversion; capital raises persistently dilute common owners; or regulatory/competitive changes impair distribution and ad monetization. Regulatory outcomes are scenario risks, not invented quantified liabilities.

Deliverables and limits

The companion files preserve all financial observations, source IDs and fetch/read status, guidance vintages, annual scenario paths, qualitative management capabilities and an explicit asset/obligation register. New AI capital returns, private investment fair values, credit-loss probabilities and October balance-sheet changes remain uncertain. No full commercial transcript is stored, no video viewing is claimed and no GOOG price fit was performed.

Meta Platforms forecast dossier

Research cutoff: 17 October 2026. Currency: USD. Financial amounts below are billions unless stated otherwise. This is a bounded evidence review, not every historical management statement. The structured files contain exact dates, units, source identifiers and scenario calculations.

Conclusion

The core advertising franchise supports strong near-term growth, but the capital and legal commitments make a simple extrapolation of 2025 margins and free cash flow unreliable. Proposed base revenue growth is 20%, 18%, 16% in the first three forecast years, then a rate fade to 2.5% by year 10. The proposed mature EBIT margin is 33%, normalized tax 20%, direct early capital-spend/D&A/working-capital assumptions (derived S:C approximately 0.34, 0.36, 0.39, followed by normalization and a terminal-consistent transition), WACC 10%, and terminal ROIC 12%. These are our assumptions, not management forecasts. Forecast year one is the rolling year after June 2026, not calendar 2026. The claims bridge remains unresolved, so these are operating-value scenarios rather than finished share-price targets.

Evidence and business mix

  • Latest reported quarter: Q2 2026, released 29 July. Revenue $60.801bn grew 28% reported and 27% in constant currency. Advertising was $59.363bn, 97.6% of revenue. Impressions grew 14% and average price 12%; daily active people were 3.6bn, up 3%. This supports an engagement/monetization explanation, not an invented standalone AI revenue stream. Other Family of Apps revenue was $1.007bn; Reality Labs revenue $0.431bn. Quarterly release
  • FY2025 revenue was $200.966bn and EBIT $83.276bn. Reality Labs lost $19.193bn on $2.207bn revenue. TTM revenue through June 2026 was $228.247bn and EBIT $86.926bn, a 38.1% margin. Quarterly standalone revenue, EBIT and SBC sums differ from filed year-to-date figures by $1m; the filed YTD-based TTM is the anchor. 2025 annual release, June filing
  • Q2 EBIT was $18.775bn, a 30.9% reported margin. The quarter included $2.400bn legal expense and $1.180bn severance; removing only those identified items gives about 36.8%. This is an analytical normalization, not reported EBIT. SBC was $7.658bn and D&A $6.356bn. Ongoing SBC remains an expense in valuation. Q2 capex including finance-lease principal was $31.078bn, leaving reported FCF only $0.784bn. Quarterly release

Guidance and management commentary

July formal guidance put Q3 revenue at $61–64bn, with an approximately 1% FX headwind; FY2026 capex at $130–145bn and expenses at $165–169bn. The August legal agreement adds approximately $10bn Q3 legal expense that was not included in July expense guidance. Other July guidance ranges were stated to be unchanged. Do not keep July's profitability interpretation without this update. July release, 26 August update

Issuer-hosted July earnings and follow-up transcripts were read, not videos watched. Management described AI improvements to engagement, ad ranking and monetization; messaging, subscriptions and business agents are additional opportunities. Capacity procurement is aimed at 2026–27 constraints, with lower visibility beyond 2028 and more flexible land/power/shell commitments. No quantified 2027 capex outlook was supplied. The CEO's 2025 personal-superintelligence letter is strategic ambition rather than a financial forecast. Earnings transcript, follow-up transcript, CEO letter

Guidance track record and management capabilities

The original next-quarter revenue range was matched to actual revenue for 12 consecutive target quarters, Q3 2023 through Q2 2026. Seven outcomes exceeded the high end, five were within range, and none were below. Mean midpoint error was +3.72%. This is evidence of conservative short-horizon revenue guidance, not proof of reliable decade-long AI returns. The original 2025 capex range of $60–65bn was repeatedly raised; actual capex including finance-lease principal was $72.215bn. Revenue accuracy and capital-spend forecasting deserve different assessments.

Mark Zuckerberg was CEO throughout this sample. Susan Li was CFO throughout, having taken office on 1 November 2022. Attribution is to the management system and business, not a personality score. The five-dimension capability file records evidence and counterexamples: strong core ad monetization and conservative quarterly revenue forecasts; uncertain new AI/Reality Labs product returns and capacity economics; historical cost leverage now facing substantial spending pressure.

Capital, accounting and claims

  • Most server/network useful lives became 5.5 years from January 2025, reducing 2025 depreciation by $2.920bn and increasing net income by $2.590bn. Longer accounting lives do not reduce cash replacement costs. 2025 annual filing, Note 1
  • June cash and marketables were $90.260bn and debt carrying value $83.664bn. Nonmarketable equity investments were $30.157bn; $13.809bn restricted cash should not be treated as freely distributable. Asset carrying values require a valuation/tax assessment, not automatic dollar-for-dollar inclusion. June filing
  • The filing reports $278.990bn not-yet-commenced lease obligations, another $68bn of July leases, and $349.310bn noncancelable contractual commitments. These categories must be checked for overlap. They belong in a cash-cost/reinvestment schedule or consistent lease treatment, not mechanically summed as debt. Cloud-capacity support of up to $14.720bn and venture residual-value guarantees are conditional exposures. June filing
  • The El Paso venture targets 1GW online in 2028. Meta owns 20%, BlackRock 80%; approximately $14bn is long-lived development cost, with servers additional. The initial lease is four years with extension options up to 20 years. Low initial equity funding does not eliminate future rent or guarantee exposure. 28 July issuer announcement
  • The proposed state settlement is approximately $18bn over ten years: about $12.7bn committed and $5.3bn conditional on specified TikTok/YouTube actions and contributions. Judicial approval was pending in the announcement. Under an illustrative equal year-end installment assumption and 10% discount rate, the committed portion is worth about $7.8bn today; this is not a disclosed payment schedule. Do not both deduct that PV and include the same cash payments in forecast FCFF. 26 August announcement

Forecast interpretation and limits

The base reaches approximately $652bn revenue in year 10, 2.85 times the June TTM base. The bear reaches $371bn; the conditional 15-year bull $1.304tn. These are scale checks, not total-addressable-market evidence. The file also shows all six combinations of 3/5 explicit years and 10/15/20 maturity horizons, as constant-S:C duration diagnostics. These diagnostic values omit the selected scenarios' final capital transition and are not identical to the selected base. Longer runway must be supported economically; it is not a free valuation uplift.

At the illustrative base settings, operating enterprise value is about $800bn before the cash/debt/investment/legal/contingent-claim bridge. Roughly 90% comes from discounted terminal value, so terminal assumptions and capital efficiency dominate the result. The bear includes fixed near-term reinvestment floors because committed construction does not disappear when ad growth slows. Those floors and lease/depreciation schedules are model gaps in a single sales-to-capital implementation.

Invalidate or lower confidence if ad growth repeatedly falls below 10%, capacity spending fails to improve monetization, normalized margin stays below 30%, spending commitments exceed modeled cash generation, or legal/venture claims crystallize beyond the scenarios. The current evidence does not establish October cash balances, the precise settlement schedule, all contract overlap or realized returns on the AI buildout. No current share price was used to fit the assumptions.

Capital and funding refinement

The first three base years now use the direct capital and cash-funding reconciliation, rather than a fixed early sales-to-capital ratio. Economic FCFF retains SBC expense; the separate cash view accounts for noncash SBC and employee share-settlement cash. The central three-year cash proxy needs about $77.8bn before interest, dividends and legal payments, versus $90.3bn June cash/marketables. This is a conditional planning range, not an additional debt deduction.

NVIDIA forecast and valuation dossier

What changes the base case

The current operating ramp warrants a steeper early revenue path than the old flat 40% input, but financing support and supplier commitments now warrant an equally explicit downside model. The latest quarter was $96.221bn revenue, 106% year-over-year growth and $63.734bn GAAP operating income. Latest TTM revenue/EBIT were $302.970bn/$197.579bn. A low reported physical-capex ratio no longer captures the whole economic commitment.

The August 26 issuer results and original Q2 filing are the primary anchors. FY2027 Q2 ended July 26. FY2027 has 53 weeks, including a 14-week Q4; this matters when comparing annual growth.

Business and trajectory

Data Center was $89.023bn, 92.5% of quarterly revenue; Edge Computing $7.198bn. Hyperscale $48.710bn and ACIE $40.313bn subdivide Data Center. Compute & Networking $88.299bn and Graphics $7.922bn are a different reportable-segment classification. Do not add across classifications. Prior market presentation was recast and one ACIE customer moved into hyperscale in Q2. On that latest recast basis, Q1 FY2027 Data Center/Edge were $75.246bn/$6.370bn, versus $41.096bn/$5.647bn in Q2 FY2026. The full preceding-quarter mix series and derivations are in evidence-NVDA.html#facts.

Annual revenue grew 125.9% in FY2024, 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026; GAAP EBIT margins were 54.1%, 62.4% and 60.4%. The latest TTM margin is 65.2%. These are extraordinary cycle/platform economics, not a credible perpetual extrapolation. Annual source-level financial history, capex, tax, R&D, SBC and capital proxies are retained in evidence-NVDA.html#facts.

Management outlook and revisions

The August 26 corrected earnings-call text gives Q3 revenue $108bn ±2%, excluding China Data Center compute. Management discussed preliminary FY2028 growth around 70%, constrained by supply. That remains an unseasoned forecast, not an actual or analyst consensus.

Rising memory costs changed the margin outlook: Q4 FY2027 gross margin 71–72%, followed by FY2028 72–73% after price increases. This should flow into EBIT forecasts. Rubin production shipments reportedly began in August, consistent with the preceding May call's Q3 start expectation; shipment timing is management-reported, not independently audited. Corporate revenue guidance, product visibility and broad customer-capex estimates have different scopes.

The November 19, 2025 Blackwell-plus-Rubin $500bn calendar-2025/2026 visibility statement cannot yet be scored against full-year corporate revenue. Industry cloud backlog, customer capex and the August third-party financing target are not NVIDIA backlog. September 10 Jensen Huang conference Q&A was read as a public transcript; no video was watched. His confidence in compute-asset fungibility and physical AI is a thesis requiring evidence, not a quantitative quarterly target.

All ten original revenue ranges were exceeded; mean signed midpoint error was +5.57%. This supports conservative short-horizon revenue guidance during this ramp, rather than exact unbiased demand prediction. Seven of ten GAAP gross-margin outcomes were inside guidance, two above and one below. FY2026 Q1 was 60.5% versus 70.6% ±0.5 points after H20 export restrictions: retain that 10.1-point miss. Non-GAAP definitions changed in FY2027 to retain SBC, so the matched margin series uses GAAP. Exact sources, actual publication dates and errors appear in evidence-NVDA.html#guidance. No longer-horizon CEO credibility score or valuation multiplier is inferred.

Cash investment, accounting and returns

Six-month CFO was $74.421bn; physical/intangible purchases $4.434bn, D&A $2.124bn and SBC $3.954bn. Receivables and inventories absorbed $34.794bn combined before other working-capital changes. Payment terms can extend 90 days to one year for investment-grade customers. Equity purchases were another $42.404bn; these are not ordinary capex, but are real capital deployed into an ecosystem linked to product demand. Reported net income includes large investment gains; use operating EBIT for enterprise valuation.

Historical book ROIC and incremental sales/capital proxies are useful diagnostics, not adjusted economic returns: they omit capitalized R&D, complete lease/guarantee exposure and a clean separation of nonoperating assets. A 2x forward incremental sales/capital assumption is therefore judgment, requiring cash-flow and capacity reconciliation. Do not release capital mechanically in a revenue contraction while purchase obligations remain.

Obligations and asset bridge: unresolved

The issuer 10-Q, Note 12 separates own-use commitments from customer support. The register in evidence-NVDA.html#judgment records measurement date, source, conditionality and proposed treatment for every following item:

  • $366bn own-use investment/procurement commitments: $279bn supply/capacity, $29bn cloud, $25bn future leases, $25bn equity investments and $8bn capex.
  • Additional $36bn AI-cloud agreements and $20bn third-party leases intended for reassignment. Capacity sales/use may reduce the former; reassignment of the latter is intended, not guaranteed.
  • $3.529bn existing land/power/shell guarantees and $712m partner escrow; default-triggered with declining exposure.
  • August $105bn SB Energy/OpenAI guarantee cap, for nine phases of 4.25GW. First phase expected FY2029; covered obligations run over 20-year leases, decline and have defined termination conditions. Another 3.8GW is discretionary. This is not $105bn funded debt, nor harmless merely because no payment is currently due.
  • $33.366bn debt; $5.494bn recognized operating leases; $986m accrued Groq consideration; $56.586bn cash/current debt securities before operating-liquidity review.
  • $42.783bn marketable equity, $47.898bn nonmarketable equity and $3.3bn equity-method investments require after-tax realizable valuation. Do not add investment gains to EBIT and then add assets again.
  • 168m outstanding unvested awards, versus 24.1bn cover shares on August 21. Unrecognized compensation $19.4bn is not award fair value.

The August 10 financing MOUs seek over $500bn of third-party capital over time. They are not NVIDIA cash, debt or signed customer revenue. Default probability, construction phase, recovery and correlation with operating downside are needed to value conditional support. Missing additional claims/assets remain null, not zero.

All scenarios fade linearly after their explicit early years to 2.5% terminal growth. Base EBIT margins are 62/59/56% in years 1–3, then fade to 45% by year 10. Years are rolling 12-month periods after July 26, not fiscal labels. Fiscal cross-check: actual H1 $177.837bn + Q3 guide $108bn + analyst Q4 $120bn gives FY2027 $405.837bn; management's 70% would imply FY2028 about $690bn. This is a cross-check, not a validated quarterly bridge.

The base's $2.18trn mature sales and bull's $4.76trn are demanding scale requirements, not concealed outputs. A 10-year base is preferred over 15/20 because customer economics beyond the current platform cycle are uncertain. The bull's longer runway tests durable full-stack expansion. Terminal ROIC requires reinvestment, rather than treating terminal profit as entirely distributable. Base WACC 11% is judgment, informed by October 16 USD10-year Treasury 5.09% and chosen ERP 4.5%; no current measured beta or credit spread is claimed. Normalize operating tax at 20% rather than automatically perpetuating management's near-term 16–18%.

Management strengths and invalidators

The evidence supports rapid product monetization, supplier coordination and operating leverage. It is weaker on the realized returns of recent financing support and strategic investments, which have not seasoned. Jensen Huang and Colette Kress led throughout the matched period, but outcomes belong to the team and environment. Export controls, customer monetization, financing deterioration, memory/power constraints, custom silicon and extended receivables are primary invalidators. Review evidence-NVDA.html#management for dimension-specific evidence and counterexamples.

Source limitations and adoption gate

Primary releases, annual/current filings, issuer-hosted call text, investor/keynote materials and a public leadership Q&A were inspected. No audio/video was watched. Some interview pages failed; no paywall bypass was attempted. Analyst consensus was not collected. evidence-NVDA.html#sources distinguishes source types and gaps. These proposals remain research illustrations until segment/fiscal, cash-investment, conditional-credit, tax/lease and share/asset bridges are reconciled. No app default was edited and no price calibration was used.

Tesla forecast dossier

Research cutoff: 17 October 2026. Currency: USD. Financial amounts are billions unless stated otherwise. Thirteen issuer shareholder updates were acquired; twelve consecutive outlook sections from Q3 2023 to Q2 2026 were reviewed for guidance policy. This is bounded coverage, not every historical statement.

Conclusion

Tesla requires an explicit capital-spending and contingent-dilution model before a renewed share-price default. The latest quarter's 26% revenue growth coexists with a 1.4% operating margin and more than $25bn planned 2026 capex. A base case of 12%, 12%, 10% initial growth and eventual 10% EBIT margin requires a recovery in vehicle economics and growth in energy/services; major Robotaxi or Optimus profits remain conditional. A constant sales-to-capital ratio cannot faithfully represent both the present buildout and later capital normalization.

The old debt input also needs a verified correction: $7.721bn is long-term debt, not total debt. The June filing adds $1.340bn current debt and $0.281bn finance leases, for $9.342bn debt plus finance leases. No application files were changed. June filing, debt table

Actual business mix and current evidence

Q2 2026 revenue was $28.236bn: automotive $20.516bn, energy $3.139bn, services/other $4.581bn. EBIT was $0.398bn, SBC $1.151bn, D&A $1.619bn, operating cash flow $4.697bn and cash capex $5.789bn. Revenue growth was 26%, automotive 23%, energy 13% and services/other 50%. TTM revenue through June was $103.619bn and EBIT $4.372bn, a 4.2% margin. Automotive was 73.0% of TTM revenue, energy 12.4%, services/other 14.6%. Services revenue is not synonymous with high-margin software. Q2 issuer update, June filing

FY2025 deliveries were 1,636,129 versus 1,789,226 in 2024 and 1,808,581 in 2023. Energy deployments grew from 14.7GWh in 2023 to 31.4GWh in 2024 and 46.7GWh in 2025. FY2025 revenue was $94.827bn and EBIT $4.355bn. 2025 update

The 2 October announcement gives Q3 2026 production of 464,391 vehicles, deliveries of 486,532 and 13.7GWh deployed. Q3 deliveries were 2.1% below Q3 2025. This is operating data only. Financial results are scheduled for 21 October, after the research cutoff; Q3 revenue, margin and cash flow are not yet known. Operating announcement

Guidance, interviews and product milestones

No formal numerical quarterly consolidated revenue or EBIT range was found in the twelve consecutive shareholder outlooks reviewed. This means no comparable quarterly revenue-guidance score is available, not a 0% accuracy score. Annual volume/energy guidance and product timelines must be assessed separately.

  • The 2023 approximately 1.8m vehicle target appears in a production outlook. Actual production was approximately 1.846m, about 2.6% above that approximate target. Deliveries are a different metric.
  • October 2024's expectation of slight delivery growth for 2024 missed: deliveries fell 1.1%. Its expectation that energy deployments would more than double was met, with 113.6% growth.
  • January 2025's return-to-growth vehicle outlook missed on both deliveries and automotive revenue. The at-least-50% energy deployment expectation was narrowly missed at 48.7%. April guidance was withdrawn amid trade-policy uncertainty; preserve that revision separately rather than erase the original promise.
  • The first-half-2025 affordable-model initial-production milestone was met by June first builds. That does not establish volume sales. Cybercab initial production in 2026 does not by itself satisfy a volume-production target. Semi/Megapack 3 volume/start milestones remain pending as of the cutoff.

The files preserve original forecast dates, definitions, revisions and outcome sources. Do not compare a selected long-range Musk product promise with Jensen Huang's short-quarter revenue range as if they were the same forecasting task.

The original World Economic Forum publisher's January 2026 interview metadata and accessible indexed transcript portions were read. Musk discussed possible public Optimus sales by the end of 2027, conditional on reliability, safety and functionality, and power constraints on AI. The full video was not watched; the page's full transcript was not accessible in rendered text. These are conditional future aspirations, not formal revenue guidance or overdue promises. Original WEF interview

A public secondary Q2 call transcript was also read. The CFO described more than $25bn 2026 capex, further growth over the following two to three years, and possible borrowing facilities up to $30bn. The latter is financing intent, not drawn debt. Remarks also explain warranty/tariff effects, subscription mix and uncertain new-product ramps. No full commercial transcript was copied; financial claims are anchored to the issuer deck and filing where available. Public transcript

The issuer's 17 July analyst survey is an analyst estimate snapshot, not management guidance and not current October consensus. It is retained only with that label. Dated survey

Management capability assessment

Elon Musk was CEO throughout the reviewed period. Vaibhav Taneja became CFO on 4 August 2023; Zachary Kirkhorn preceded him. Outcome attribution must also consider engineering, operations, policy, price competition and product mix. Appointment filing

The evidence supports successful energy capacity expansion and some initial production milestones. It is weaker for recent annual vehicle-demand forecasts and for assuming that announced autonomy/robotics capacity will translate promptly into profitable customer revenue. Cost control is mixed: high revenue growth has not produced consolidated operating leverage. Capital allocation into autonomy, robotics and outside investments has substantial optionality but not yet an observable incremental return sufficient to support a blanket credibility premium. The capability matrix provides a counterexample and confidence level for each dimension.

Capital, financing and dilution

  • More than $25bn gross 2026 capex is stated in the June filing. Net reinvestment is gross capex minus economic depreciation plus working-capital and other operating investment. It cannot be equated directly to capex, and it cannot fall automatically to zero when revenue is flat. June filing, MD&A
  • June cash/investments were $43.524bn. SpaceX investment carrying value was $3.007bn on $2.002bn cost; the $1.005bn mark-up was below EBIT. Digital assets were $0.674bn. These are separate nonoperating assets, with valuation, tax and liquidity uncertainty. Nonredeemable NCI was $0.607bn and redeemable NCI $0.054bn. June filing
  • Approximately 304m 2018 CEO options were exercised during Q2, with roughly 17.5m shares used in net exercise settlement; resulting restricted shares have a January 2028 service condition. The 96m interim 2025 shares were forfeited in April. Do not count the forfeited interim award or the exercised option claim again. Cover-page common shares were 3,949,547,394 on 16 July. June filing, awards and cover page
  • The 2025 CEO award covers up to 423,743,904 restricted performance shares in twelve tranches, requiring market-cap and operating milestones, service periods and an offset of $334.09 per share unless paid in cash. It is neither an unconditional 423.7m extra shares nor a zero economic claim. Issued/restricted shares, potential forfeiture, offsets and share-count treatment must be reconciled before valuation. June filing, compensation note

Forecast proposal and what would invalidate it

The base's 12%, 12%, 10% initial revenue growth is an analytical mix-based recovery assumption. Year one is the rolling year after June 2026, not calendar 2026. At the TTM mix, roughly 8% automotive growth and 20% growth in energy and services imply about 11.2% consolidated growth. Growth fades to 2.5% by year 10, reaching about $211bn revenue. The 10% target operating margin, 25% normalized tax, 12% WACC and 12% terminal ROIC are judgments, not management guidance. A 15-year conditional bull reaches approximately $686bn and requires materially more software-heavy paid autonomy economics.

Near-term capital intensity is modeled separately from eventual normalization, with a final fade to capital efficiency consistent with terminal ROIC. The structured scenario file preserves the highly capital-intensive constant-S:C diagnostic as well as the proposed normalization path. This distinction is material: ongoing heavy capital spending without high-margin autonomous services consumes most operating value. The bear retains explicit near-term investment floors. A negative operating-value diagnostic signals that the assumed investment program is not self-funding; equity has abandonment, financing and business-model options that a mechanical negative DCF does not capture.

All six 3/5-year early-phase and 10/15/20-year horizon combinations are shown as duration sensitivities. Twenty years of elevated growth is not justified merely because the controls permit it. No share price was used to fit inputs.

The base fails if vehicle volume/price economics do not recover, energy costs and warranties erode margins, capital spending stays elevated without cash returns, or autonomy cannot demonstrate paid utilization and acceptable safety/intervention performance. The historical promise sample is bounded, older autonomy promises were not exhaustively reconstructed, and future milestones remain unscored until their deadlines and definitions are observable.

Capital and funding refinement

The first three base years now use explicit capital-spend, D&A and working-capital scenarios. The central cash proxy requires about $49.7bn over three years, versus $43.5bn June cash/short-term investments, before reserve and award-settlement requirements. The resulting core-business-plus-buildout operating value is low because the case funds a large program without presuming major autonomy/robotics profits. It is a diagnostic of required investment returns, not a complete probability-weighted Tesla value or a final per-share target.

Final capital-transition refinement

The selected base extends explicit capex/D&A/WC through year7 rather than assuming investment drops abruptly after year3. Gross capex34/38/42/38/35/34/34bn and D&A8/11/15/20/24/27/28bn are analytical budgets, conditional on commissioning and utilization. Years8–10 normalize to terminal ROIC with a disclosed derived component bridge. This produces about $3.064bn illustrative operating value before assets/claims, superseding the earlier $11bn calculation. Holding year4 net reinvestment at $29bn would reduce it by another $6.037bn. This fragile core-plus-buildout scenario is not a complete probability-weighted Tesla equity valuation. See the full capital bridge and stress test in evidence-TSLA.html#judgment.
