The complete original narrative follows. Its dated proposal language is preserved. The selected executable case and any later capital overlays are shown separately in the evidence pages.

Coherent (COHR): forecast and valuation dossier

Decision: A steeper, shorter early-growth profile is better supported than the old flat 25% assumption. Propose 45%, 30%, 20% growth for FY2027–FY2029 and a ten-year total maturity horizon, with 20% mature EBIT margin. Treat this as an operating proposal; do not publish a refreshed per-share value until cash, minority interests and dilution are reconciled.

Cutoff: October 17, 2026. Fiscal years end June 30. Unless stated otherwise, financial figures are USD millions. The latest actual quarter is June 2026, released August 12; the annual report was filed August 14. First-quarter FY2027 results were not yet in this evidence set. Forecasts below are our analysis, not issuer guidance or consensus.

What changed and what drives growth

Annual revenue increased from $4,707.7m in FY2024 to $5,810.1m in FY2025 and $7,118.2m in FY2026. Latest-quarter revenue was $2,045.5m, up 33.8% year on year and 13.3% sequentially. Datacenter and Communications reached $5,274.6m for FY2026, approximately 74.1% of revenue, versus $3,755.2m a year earlier. Industrial declined to $1,843.6m from $2,055.0m, with portfolio sales affecting comparability. Treat AI optics as the principal current growth driver rather than extrapolating equal growth across both segments.

Management's August 12 formal next-quarter revenue range is $2,200–2,400m, with non-GAAP gross margin of 39.5–41.5% and EPS of $1.85–2.05. In the readable call, management also expected its first quarter above $3bn by the end of FY2027. That is a conditional exit-quarter expectation, not a $12bn annual forecast. The same discussion covers InP capacity expansion and OCS/CPO opportunities. Orders extending into later years improve visibility but do not remove qualification, shipment or customer acceptance conditions.

Our FY2027 base revenue of $10.321bn is consistent with a ramp from the formal first-quarter range toward that potential exit pace. Growth in FY2028 and FY2029 is judgment, not a management forecast. Three early years are preferable to locking peak scarcity-driven growth in for five. The bull case separately tests five years of stronger optical-content expansion.

Earnings quality and capital requirements

FY2026 reported EBIT was $897.9m. Removing $124.1m of business-sale gains gives a simple operating normalization of $773.8m, or 10.9% of sales; this calculation does not claim to remove every unusual item. Q4 GAAP operating margin was 12.4%, compared with 21.8% non-GAAP. Segment profit is not consolidated EBIT and must not replace it in the DCF.

Cash from operations fell to $79.5m from $633.6m while PPE cash spending rose to $1,102.9m from $440.8m. FY2026 depreciation was $241.6m, intangible amortization $280.3m and cash-flow-statement SBC $186.5m. Inventory consumed roughly $1,183m of cash; payables provided $748.5m, while other operating assets consumed $408.3m. Inventory ended at about $2,581m. Strong bookings and adjusted earnings therefore have not yet translated into comparable free cash flow.

Use a staged EBIT path of 17%, 19%, then 20%, retaining continuing SBC, depreciation and R&D. Early incremental sales-to-capital ratios of 0.8, 1.0 and 1.25 deliberately recognize build-out and working-capital demands. These ratios measure incremental sales relative to net operating reinvestment, not sales divided by gross capex. The later ratio must reconcile with terminal margin, tax and ROIC; the supplied annual schedule does so.

The old extracted book ROIC proxy is not decision-ready: disposal gains, a low reported effective tax rate, acquired intangibles and changes in the equity structure affect it. A 12% terminal ROIC and 24% normalized tax rate are judgments, not a verified through-cycle return. Likewise, the 10.5% base WACC is a scenario input, not a newly measured beta/spread estimate.

Contracts, concentration and capital claims

The March 2 NVIDIA $2bn equity investment and commercial capacity arrangement provide financing and demand visibility, but investment proceeds are not sales. The annual report describes potential equipment, labor and working-capital investment through 2030; a zero recorded liability does not establish a zero future cash requirement. Two customers represented 20% and 12% of annual revenue. Firm supplier purchases can coexist with customer retiming or cancellation risk.

June unrestricted cash and short-term investments total $1,987.0m, separate from $606.4m of restricted cash. Book debt is $3,222.2m and minority interest $334.7m. Existing Series B preferred converted in FY2026 Q2; retaining its old claim after counting conversion shares would double-count it. The August 27 executive PSU awards introduce another contingent equity claim with $100m aggregate target value. This is compensation, not an operating target; eventual award shares and fair value remain unbridged.

Management interpretation

Jim Anderson joined as CEO on June 3, 2024, so all eight original quarterly forecasts in this review were issued under his tenure. The stronger quarterly record supports short-horizon revenue planning. It does not establish that portfolio restructuring, capital spending or acquired assets will earn an adequate long-run return. The demand, product, capacity, cost and capital-allocation assessments below deliberately retain counterexamples.

Primary financial evidence: FY2026 annual report; FY2026-Q4 results and next-quarter outlook. Exact fact/source links are in evidence-COHR.html#facts and evidence-COHR.html#sources.

Invalidators and next evidence

  1. Q1 FY2027 shipments fall materially below the $2.2bn guide floor or the fiscal-year exit ramp is delayed.
  2. Inventory/payables growth continues to consume cash without matching shipment and collection growth.
  3. InP yield or customer qualification limits prevent the stated capacity ramp.
  4. Industrial weakness offsets datacenter gains, or new optical architectures shift content to competitors.
  5. New capacity/purchase commitments earn below-cost returns despite reported revenue growth.

Coverage and limitations

current primary financial sources verified through cutoff; bounded event coverage.

Public transcripts were used for summarized management statements, not copied wholesale; no accounts, purchases or paywall bypasses were used. Sources were available as of the cutoff, but this is not a claim to have read every filing, interview or event. Lumentum (LITE): forecast and valuation dossier

Decision: Replace the old smooth 35% early-growth assumption with a front-loaded 70%, 35%, 25% FY2027–FY2029 proposal over a ten-year maturity horizon. Use 25% mature EBIT margin, below the current adjusted peak. The operating case can be considered for renewal, but the convertible settlement and dilution bridge is still necessary before a per-share valuation.

Cutoff: October 17, 2026. FY2026 ended June 27; results were released August 11 and the annual report filed August 17. Figures are USD millions unless specified. Next-quarter guidance remains pending at the cutoff. Our scenarios are neither management guidance nor analyst consensus.

Operating trajectory and revenue mix

Annual revenue was $1,359.2m in FY2024, $1,645.0m in FY2025 and $3,014.0m in FY2026. EBIT moved from losses of $434.0m and $180.1m to positive $524.8m. Q4 revenue reached $1,006.3m, up 109.3% year on year and 24.5% sequentially. Components contributed $649.4m and Systems $356.9m; the preceding quarter was $533.3m and $275.1m. Both product groups accelerated, rather than all growth being confined to one small pilot product.

Formal Q1 FY2027 guidance is revenue of $1,225–1,275m, non-GAAP operating margin of 39.5–40.5%, and adjusted EPS of $4.05–4.35. Our $5.124bn FY2027 revenue base begins near the annualized first-quarter midpoint, while allowing growth, shipment variability and concentration risk. The following two years have no matching issuer annual forecast and are our judgment.

The latest readable call describes a 50% year-on-year EML unit-output expansion by December 2026 and later capacity including Greensboro revenue beginning in early 2028. OCS and CPO create additional opportunities, but backlog is not current revenue. The February OCS backlog and CPO delivery expectations are useful indicators only when matched to customer qualification, delivery, acceptance and recognized revenue. Sustained margins also depend on pricing as supply expands.

Profit, cash and reinvestment

Q4 GAAP gross margin was 47.4% and operating margin 27.8%, versus non-GAAP figures of 50.4% and 36.6%. Annual EBIT of $524.8m is positive even though net loss was $6,935.1m: the $7,756.6m debt-extinguishment loss is a financing item. It should not destroy operating EBIT in a DCF, and its economic cost to common holders should not disappear from the financing/claims bridge.

FY2026 CFO was $751.4m and PPE cash spending $451.3m, compared with $126.3m and $231.0m in FY2025. Depreciation was $128.8m, intangible amortization/write-offs $138.2m, and SBC $170.2m. Receivables and inventory absorbed $270.4m and $228.4m. Purchase obligations of $2,354.4m, including $2,112.5m within one year, make future working-capital and capacity funding important even after the recent CFO improvement.

Our EBIT margin path is 30%, 29%, 27%, then 25%. It assumes a strong current mix and utilization benefit but fades exceptional pricing, rather than perpetuating next-quarter non-GAAP guidance. Continuing SBC, R&D and depreciation remain expenses. Early incremental sales-to-capital ratios are 1.1, 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6, then fade to terminal consistency. The ratios still need an explicit procurement, capex, depreciation and working-capital schedule.

A 22% normalized tax rate and 14% terminal ROIC are judgments. Reported tax, debt losses, acquisitions and conversion accounting make a simple historical net-income return misleading. There is no claim that 14% has been proven through a full investment and replacement cycle. The 11.5% WACC is a transparent scenario assumption, not a fresh market-beta estimate.

Financing and concentration are central

June cash of $2,043.5m and investments of $694.9m must be rolled against note settlements. Book debt totaled $1,637.4m, including $1,544.6m of convertible carrying value and $92.8m of term loans. Convertible principal was $1,554.3m. All note series were current because holders could elect conversion; this is not equivalent to all principal being contractually due on that date.

As of August 14, $757.8m principal had been submitted for conversion. Principal must settle in cash, while excess conversion value may use cash, shares or both. Capped calls, early settlements and inducement transactions require series-specific treatment. A model cannot subtract the full note claim and also include full if-converted shares without a consistent reconciliation.

NVIDIA's March investment created approximately 2.9m preferred shares that are economically common-like, with one-for-one common conversion and no economic preference. They should not be modeled as both a $2bn senior deduction and common-equivalent shares. The two largest customers represented 26.6% and 15% of annual revenue. Much of the order book lacks enduring volume commitments, so customer concentration and rapid product transitions remain material risks.

Management interpretation

Michael Hurlston's appointment was announced February 3, 2025 and became effective February 7. Several forecasts in the eight-quarter sample predate his tenure, including the FY2025 Q3 guide issued February 6. Attribution therefore distinguishes his team's later execution from inherited designs, capacity and earlier guidance. June 3, 2025 guidance was raised before the quarter closed; a February 3 preliminary revenue result is a post-period update, not a new ex-ante forecast.

Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI): forecast and valuation dossier

Decision: Keep a conditional capacity-ramp scenario rather than install a confident new default. A calendar-2026 revenue bridge and explicit factory/funding/dilution model are necessary. The illustrative base uses approximately $1.1bn in 2026 and growth of 150%, 60%, 35% in 2027–2029, but this is a demanding execution scenario, not an issuer forecast for those years. Existing conservative staged sensitivities should remain visible.

Cutoff: October 17, 2026. Calendar-year reporter. Latest actuals cover June 30, released August 6; the investor deck was posted September 21 but explicitly dates its outlook to August 6. Financial amounts are USD millions unless specified. The latest completed ATM financing is dated October 5. There are no analyst-estimate inputs in the proposed scenarios.

Revenue ramp: what is actual and what is conditional

Revenue grew from $217.6m in 2023 to $249.4m in 2024 and $455.7m in 2025. Operating losses were $41.3m, $70.9m and $54.6m respectively. Q2 2026 revenue of $191.922m compared with $102.952m a year earlier and $151.144m in Q1. Datacenter contributed $107.662m, CATV $80.578m, telecom $3.411m and other $0.271m. Datacenter is now about 56% of quarterly revenue; a single blended optical-growth assumption obscures CATV exposure and product-transition risk.

Formal Q3 revenue guidance is $255–290m, non-GAAP gross margin 29–30.5%, and adjusted EPS $0.11–0.26. The approximately $1.1bn annual outlook is separately quantified management guidance. With H1 revenue of $343.066m and Q3 at its midpoint, it requires Q4 revenue of $484.434m, more than 2.5 times Q2. The strong quarterly forecasting record does not make that acceleration automatic.

The issuer presentation targets combined 800G/1.6T monthly capacity of 650,000 units in Q4 2026 and 930,000 in Q4 2027. Nameplate capacity is not shipments or paid revenue. Installation, customer qualification, yields, components, order allocation and collections must all occur. The latest readable call reports Q2 800G revenue of only $12.8m and describes future 1.6T qualification/delivery. Timing descriptions for a large order differ within the transcript, so no single precise delivery schedule is imposed here. The August 18 CFO interview describes domestic automation and laser integration as advantages; the valuation does not assume a future regulatory ban on competitors or a guaranteed domestic premium.

Operating profit has not caught up

Q2 GAAP operating loss was $24.727m. Non-GAAP net income of $5.5m and EPS of $0.06 should not be mistaken for operating profitability: the presentation still reports a non-GAAP operating loss of about $10.3m. Q2 GAAP gross margin was 27.7%, versus 29.8% adjusted. H1 operating loss was $37.718m. Cost execution and revenue forecasting need separate assessments.

H1 CFO was negative $73.781m. Cash PPE purchases of $335.132m, capital prepayments of $289.744m and land of $8.581m sum to $633.457m of capital cash uses. D&A was only $19.729m and SBC $9.254m. Receivables consumed $69.649m and inventories $94.092m, partly offset by $142.156m from payables. Net PPE of $697.086m includes $168.805m construction in progress, while capital prepayments stand at $324.045m. This spending creates future depreciation and operating obligations; it is not excess cash and should not be counted again on equipment delivery.

Our conditional EBIT path of 6%, 12%, then 15% requires much stronger utilization and mix. Early incremental sales-to-capital of 0.6, 0.85 and 1.1 is only a funding diagnostic. Mature tax of 25%, ROIC of 11% and WACC of 13.5% are judgments. Current losses establish no positive economic ROIC; the base intentionally has a terminal return below the funding cost. A large revenue outcome can still destroy capital.

Financing and customer-linked dilution

June cash was $499.737m, bank debt $58.915m and vendor bank acceptances $33.940m. Convertible principal was $124.925m versus book value $129.142m and disclosed June fair value $445.1m. The deck excludes the note from its debt presentation because management expects stock settlement; that convention does not remove the economic claim. Use mutually exclusive claim/dilution treatments and reconcile vendor financing with working capital.

The October 5 completed ATM adds about $588m net and 5.695m shares. June cash plus those proceeds is not current cash because factory, property and lease spending continued. The known-transaction share calculation of 90.601m is not an independently verified October outstanding count. Houston leases, the September property purchase and Ningbo's ten-year lease must enter the forward cash model.

Amazon's warrant can cover up to 7.945399m shares at $23.6956; only 1.324233m were initially vested. Later vesting depends on purchases, with a $4bn threshold. That threshold is not guaranteed revenue. Contra-revenue, vesting and dilution must be modeled without double-charging the same warrant economics. Existing employee RSUs and PSUs add separate claims.

Management interpretation

Founder/CEO Thompson Lin and CFO Stefan Murry led throughout the reviewed period. The presentation's 28-plus-year company tenure is not assumed to mean that many years continuously in the same title. Their revenue guidance record is useful, while product delivery, factory utilization, cash conversion and allocation of expansion capital remain less proven. Earlier capacity expectations and profitability misses are retained rather than selecting only recent revenue successes.

Nebius (NBIS): forecast and valuation dossier

Decision: Withhold a renewed stand-alone base valuation until a specialist capacity, customer-advance, lease and financing model exists. The supplied operating scenarios are useful stress tests, not decision-ready equity defaults. Our conditional base uses $3.2bn calendar-2026 revenue and $9.6bn/$17.28bn/$25.056bn in 2027–2029, with 18% mature EBIT margin. That trajectory does not establish financeability or common-equity value.

Cutoff: October 17, 2026. Calendar-year reporter. Latest financials cover June 30 and were published August 12. Annual financials were filed April 30. Later financing and corporate announcements were reviewed through October 1. USD millions unless specified; power is identified in GW or MW. ARR, annual revenue, total contract value and RPO are kept separate.

A new operating perimeter

The Russian-business divestment in July 2024 and Toloka deconsolidation in 2025 make old Yandex growth and margins poor comparables. Recast continuing revenue was $91.5m in 2024 and $529.8m in 2025. The four 2025 quarters were $50.9m, $105.1m, $146.1m and $227.7m. Q1 2026 revenue reached $399.0m; Q2 reached $582.3m, with AI cloud contributing $574.9m, about 98% of group revenue. TripleTen and Avride remain in consolidated economics, while private investments require separate treatment.

Formal 2026 guidance began in the February 12 call at $3.0–3.4bn revenue, approximately 40% group adjusted EBITDA margin, and $7–9bn December AI-cloud ARR. ARR means final-month AI-cloud revenue multiplied by 12; it is not the year's recognized revenue. The range was reaffirmed in May and August. H1 actual revenue of $981.3m leaves $2,218.7m for H2 to reach the revenue midpoint. No 2027 formal revenue guide is imported into our scenario.

Management increased 2026 capex from $16–20bn in February to $20–25bn on May 13, explaining that spending supports capacity contributing in H1 2027. That is a change in the funding and timing burden, not just a higher revenue forecast. A contracted-power target of 5GW at year-end differs from the 0.8–1.0GW connected-power target and from fully active, billable capacity. The March 4 issuer-hosted leadership interview reinforces the integrated hardware/cloud strategy while acknowledging the realities of the development pipeline.

Contract visibility has conditions

June RPO was $37,490.6m, with 36% expected in the next 24 months and 40% in the following 24. It includes deferred and unbilled noncancelable revenue subject to recognition constraints, and excludes short-duration contracts. This is not the same measure as every announced TCV or every booking.

The Meta agreement signed March 13 and filed March 16 contains $12bn of dedicated five-year orders beginning deployments in early 2027, plus a potential $15bn backstop for eligible unsold capacity. Third-party revenue on those clusters and Meta purchases of the same unsold capacity cannot both be counted. Service commitments, termination provisions and discounts for late delivery apply. RPO and headline contract values must be reconciled rather than summed as independent assets.

Customer advances improve funding, but June deferred revenue of $5,975.2m represents future performance and can include refundable balances. Management's attractive deal-payback statements are estimates under its utilization, pricing and cost assumptions. They are not evidence of consolidated through-cycle ROIC or unconditional cash available to common shareholders.

Capital, depreciation and cash quality

FY2025 continuing CFO was $401.9m against $4,066m of PPE/intangible cash purchases. Deferred revenue added $1,565.8m of CFO while receivables consumed $714.6m. D&A was $417.9m and SBC $83.2m; $1,057.7m of purchased PPE/intangibles had not yet been paid. The newer H1 2026 CFO of $4,504.1m is largely explained by $4,395m of deferred-revenue inflow. H1 PPE/intangible cash spending was $8,130.3m, acquisition cash $251.6m, and financing cash inflow $9,160.4m. The H1 supplemental statement also reports $973.3m of acquired PPE/intangibles not yet paid, matching June-end PPE trade payables. This is not additional immediate H1 cash spending. Reconcile opening payables, cash payments, closing payables and other adjustments before comparing accrual capex with a cash funding model.

H1 EBIT remained negative $303.9m, with D&A of $471.7m and SBC of $137.8m, including $74.9m acquisition-related SBC. Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $236.2m and AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA margin of 49.7% therefore do not equal operating profit. The prospective server/network life change from four to five years lowers accounting depreciation; it does not prove that replacement economics improved.

Net PPE is $13,045.2m, including $7,836.4m not yet in use. As assets enter service, depreciation and ongoing operating costs rise. Signed leases not yet commenced add $12,054.1m of undiscounted payments, with $612.4m prepaid; recognized operating lease liabilities are another $1,625.3m. Minimum power commitments total $5,324.1m. These are not all debt deductions to add mechanically, but they cannot disappear because facilities are not yet active.

Our first-year sales-to-capital ratio of 0.30 implies approximately $21.3bn net reinvestment in 2027. The separate $20–30bn gross-capex and $3.5–6bn depreciation ranges are our stress inputs, not issuer guidance. Model GPU cohorts, useful lives, maintenance, datacenter construction, customer advances, rent and power before relying on FCFF. The 18% mature margin and 12% terminal ROIC are conditional judgments; a 15.5% WACC recognizes substantial financing and competitive risk.

The common-equity bridge is unresolved

June cash was $8,042.1m, with $1,056m restricted. Convertibles had $8,499m carrying value, $10,041.8m nominal maturity amounts and $20,823.7m disclosed fair value. Those are different measurement bases. July introduced a $775m secured facility. August closed $5.75bn of new original-principal notes and exchanged $800m old original principal for approximately 15.8m shares. Accretion, proceeds, fees, repayments and conversion optionality must be rolled on consistent bases.

The 21.065936m NVIDIA pre-funded warrants are effectively paid common equity, with a $0.0001 strike. Basic EPS already includes them, while legal common shares do not; count them once. The June legal count also differs from weighted-average EPS and contains acquisition shares with distinct vesting treatment. An authorization to issue shares is not actual issuance.

ClickHouse's $1,517.7m carrying value reflects a valuation adjustment and security/illiquidity terms, not a simple stale ownership percentage times a headline funding-round value. Toloka preferred is carried at $86.5m. Avride SAFE/milestone liabilities of $178.1m, Tavily holdback/earnout of $19m, and minority claims require consistent subsidiary treatment. The October Inferize announcement does not disclose purchase terms; zero consideration cannot be assumed.

Management interpretation

Assess Arkady Volozh and the post-divestment team on the new Nebius business. Engineering and product integration have evidence, and financing access has been substantial. Commercial forecasting improved after December 2024 ARR of $90m missed the original $170–190m range. Year-end 2025 active power reached approximately 170MW against a 100MW target, although the distinct 220MW connected-power outcome was not independently resolved. Capacity activation, lifecycle returns, dilution and the ability to monetize differentiation remain open. No generic CEO confidence score is warranted.

Primary financial evidence: FY2025 annual report, continuing operations recast; June 2026 interim financial statements and notes. Exact fact/source links are in evidence-NBIS.html#facts and evidence-NBIS.html#sources.

Invalidators and next evidence

  1. Connected and active MW lag contracted power; customer acceptance delays billable utilization.
  2. The $7–9bn December 2026 ARR or $3–3.4bn full-year revenue range is missed or metric definitions change.
  3. Customer prepayments are delayed, refunded or insufficient for capex and lease commitments.
  4. GPU refresh cycles are shorter than accounting lives, or realized rental prices fall as capacity supply grows.
  5. Meta backstop conditions, late delivery or contract termination reduce expected cash recovery.
  6. New financing, collateral restrictions or conversion dilution absorbs most common-equity residual.

Coverage and limitations

June 2026 interim notes and post-quarter announcements through October 1 reviewed; eight consecutive reporting events covered. Original October 18, 2024 investor-deck forecasts recovered and matched.. No matched quarterly revenue-range series was identified. Annual revenue and ARR are recorded separately. Latest official webcasts were not watched. Shareholder letters and selected readable public transcripts were reviewed. Asset URL cache-buster timestamps are not publication dates. Third-party transcripts can mislabel speakers or numerals. Primary documents take precedence. No full commercial transcript copied.

The source ledger distinguishes readable primary filings/decks/letters, readable third-party transcripts and reused previously verified extracts. Dates refer to publication/event dates rather than URL cache timestamps. Public transcripts were used for summarized management statements, not copied wholesale; no accounts, purchases or paywall bypasses were used. Sources were available as of the cutoff, but this is not a claim to have read every filing, interview or event. Inherited historical series preserve original units and provenance and are not an as-known-then backtest.

Micron (MU): forecast and valuation dossier

As of 17 October 2026. USD millions in JSON; narrative uses USD billions where marked. Research and analytical scenarios, not a price target. No price calibration or CEO valuation multiplier.

Decision summary

Preserve the reported FY2026 revenue of $133.188bn and GAAP EBIT of $99.340bn. They are real reported results, but an exceptional pricing-cycle endpoint. A flat 8% growth forecast from that annual base misses the much higher exit rate, while perpetuating the latest margin makes scarcity permanent. The preferred analytical base explicitly captures another boom year, then a price/capacity normalization in FY2029–2030. The date of normalization is a judgment, not management guidance.

Use five individually modeled early years and ten years to mature economics. The base reaches a 35% EBIT margin and 12% terminal ROIC, with substantial replacement/reinvestment spending. Refundable customer deposits, tax-payment timing, contingent grants and award dilution prevent an unqualified equity/per-share conclusion. Keep existing release gates.

1. Business, mix and the unusual starting point

Micron sells DRAM, NAND and related memory/storage products across cloud, other data-center, mobile/client and automotive/embedded applications. FY2026 product revenue was DRAM $100.679bn, NAND $31.785bn and other, mainly NOR, $0.724bn. Business-unit revenue was CMBU $43.085bn, CDBU $37.592bn, MCBU $36.601bn and AEBU $15.886bn, plus $0.024bn other. Segment-profit measures exclude some consolidated expenses; they must not replace GAAP EBIT. FY2026 10-K, notes16/20

The annual period ended September 3 and contained 53 weeks. Revenue rose 256% from FY2025, far faster than physical bit growth. The filing attributes approximately 180% DRAM and 200% NAND average selling-price increases, versus mid-20s bit growth. This is predominantly a price-and-mix step-up, not capacity that can be compounded indefinitely. Q4 revenue alone was $54.229bn. The business now exits the year well above its $33.297bn average quarter. Annual filing, September 30 results

2. Cash conversion, reinvestment and return quality

FY2026 gross profit was $107.504bn, R&D $5.650bn and SBC $1.333bn. CFO minus gross capex was $58.963bn. Management's adjusted FCF was $62.308bn because net capex was $27.367bn after $3.316bn cash incentives and $0.029bn asset-sale proceeds. The $12.747bn customer-deposit financing inflow is outside operating FCF. Do not use adjusted FCF and then add grant cash again. FY2026 filing and cash-flow reconciliation

PP&E was $63.310bn, including meaningful construction and equipment not yet in service. Incentives reduced asset carrying value by $10.930bn cumulatively and benefited FY2026 operating income by $0.901bn. Gross investment, cash grants, accounting recognition and net-basis future D&A are different schedules. A sharp future revenue decline will not allow automatic sale of fabs at book value. Tax expense was $14.761bn on $99.671bn pretax income, but $9.820bn noncurrent income-tax payable creates a separate cash-timing question. Filing notes7/15/18

The starting operating-NWC proxy is trade receivables $31.793bn + inventories $10.372bn − AP/accruals $22.605bn = $19.560bn. This deliberately simple proxy is not a complete GAAP operating-NWC reconciliation; it excludes customer returns/pricing liabilities and government receivables. Future ratios must be stress-tested, and bridge cash must not be treated as all surplus. A clean comparable historical ROIC is not asserted: peak pricing, grants, cash investments, customer financing and construction in progress materially change the denominator. Terminal ROIC is a tested forward assumption, not reported ROE.

Contract coverage is conditional

At September 3, remaining performance obligations were $134bn, approximately a quarter expected within twelve months and all within five years. The measure uses committed volumes and minimum prices, excludes contracts with only variable consideration and original terms of one year or less, and is not total expected revenue. Nearly all of roughly$13bn deposits are scheduled to return in 2029–2031; default remedies may reduce customer repayment rights. $7bn letters of credit provide contingent recovery, not current cash or revenue. Filing note16

By September 30 management reported26 strategic agreements, estimated to cover over35% of revenue through 2030; three-quarters of that estimated SCA revenue had defined pricing, largely bands, while the remainder was periodically market-priced. Customer financial commitments of $32bn are not the same as received deposits or reported RPO. Most CY2027 HBM bits were contracted at higher year-over-year prices, but this does not mean all products are sold out at permanent pricing. June remarks described16 agreements and a different, later-than-quarter-end deal set; those dates must not be merged. Q4 remarks, Q3 remarks

Management's announced capacity schedule includes Idaho1 and Tongluo during 2027, Idaho2/Japan/Singapore NAND during 2028, and New York first output in 2030. Initial output is not mature usable capacity. Our later price reset reflects a plausible combination of those additions, competitor response, bit-density progress and customer inventory, rather than a claim that management predicts oversupply. Capitalization and maintenance policy

Reported R&D remains expensed; no synthetic research asset, amortization add-back or starting EBIT rewrite is used. A later capitalization choice must adjust both earnings and invested capital consistently. SBC remains expensed. Maintenance/technology-refresh capex is not separately disclosed: D&A is a consistency proxy, not a claim that accounting depreciation equals economic replacement. After year5, D&A is assumed at18% of sales, with no additional grant cash. Base year10 gross capex is $50.09bn versus D&A $38.66bn; positive growth still requires additional capital. Tool inflation, obsolescence and uncommenced leases can require more cash than this proxy; the downside does not assume immediate factory liquidation. Cash-flow capitalization/lease reconciliation remains a final implementation gate.

Market-source provenance: common market-input assumptions, October 2026 US Treasury table.

Treatment: Add verified nonoperating liquid assets only after minimum operating cash and claims reconciliation; do not use liquidity75,480 that includes restricted cash and undrawn revolver. Status: reported composition verified; excess-cash designation open. Source

CHIPS agreements also restrict capital returns: ordinary recurring dividends are permitted; special/one-time dividends face a five-year restriction from December 9, 2024, and repurchases after the initial two-year period remain subject to financial/other conditions. A stated intention to increase returns after December 9, 2026 is not an unconditional distribution of all cash. This matters to any assumption that shareholders instantly receive the liquid-asset balance. Filing note15

6. Management capabilities, with limits

Sanjay Mehrotra has been CEO sinceMay 2017 and chairman sinceJanuary 2025; Mark Murphy CFO sinceApril 2022. August 2026 expanded Bhatia/DeBoer operating/technology roles are organizational changes with limited outcome history. The same leadership era includes the FY2023 downturn. No reputation score is assigned.

  • Demand forecasting (medium confidence): Strong near-term visibility in the observed boom; through-cycle forecasting remains uncertain. Evidence/outcome: 8 consecutive revenue outcomes at or above original midpoint; six above original range. SCAs make portions of minimum demand/pricing enforceable. FY2026Q2 and Q3 revenue exceeded original midpoints by roughly 27.6% and 23.7%, indicating material underforecasting during scarcity. Counterevidence: FY2023 operating loss and earlier inventory correction show cyclicality persists. FY2025Q2 gross margin was below midpoint; recent sample omits a completed downturn. Customer purchases to fulfill commitments can build inventories and amplify the next bust.
  • Product delivery (medium-high confidence): Recent execution has tangible shipment/qualification evidence; next-generation wins remain conditional. Evidence/outcome: HBM4 entered volume production in FY2026. 1-gamma and G9 are largest production nodes as of Q4; data-center SSD and server-memory products shipping. Mix and share opportunity are real, but FY2026 revenue growth was dominated by ASP. Counterevidence: Sampling/custom-HBM4E design work is not production revenue. 2027 node volume-production milestones are not yet achieved.
  • Capacity execution (medium confidence): Multiple construction milestones are visible; future US/Japan/Singapore ramps still require yield and schedule proof. Evidence/outcome: FY2026 gross PP&E cash spending $30.712bn; net PP&E $63.310bn. ID1 mid-2027, ID2 late-2028, New York 2030 plans extend capacity visibility. FY2026 supply expanded in mid-20s bit terms, far below nominal revenue increase. Counterevidence: Initial wafer output precedes meaningful run-rate by quarters. Grants, construction and tools add execution/financing exposure during a price downturn.
  • Cost control (high for attribution; medium for durability confidence): Manufacturing progress supports economics, but peak margins mostly reflect price rather than permanent cost advantage. Evidence/outcome: FY2026 DRAM ASP approximately +180%, NAND +200%, versus mid-20s bit growth. GAAP margin improves sharply; Q4 incentive compensation and community investment raised expenses. No basis for assigning all 74.6% FY2026 EBIT margin to management skill. Counterevidence: Q4 operating expense exceeded originally guided level after compensation decisions. Cost absorption and lagged inventory expense change as output/utilization normalizes.
  • Capital allocation (medium confidence): Deleveraging and financial flexibility improved; unprecedented capacity commitment remains untested across a full cycle. Evidence/outcome: FY2026 debt repayment $10.043bn; stock repurchases $650m; $1.333bn SBC remains an economic cost. Customer deposits and grants supplement operating cash. Balance-sheet strength rose, but $12.747bn refundable deposits are not unencumbered economic surplus. Counterevidence: $10.8bn longer-term purchase commitments; cost and subsidy clawback exposure. 100% excess-cash return intention is not a defined guaranteed distribution.

Source mapping, tenure and evidence are in evidence-MU.html#management. Capability affects execution timing, cost assumptions and scenario width; it does not earn a mechanical valuation multiplier.

7. What changes the conclusion

Monitor realized DRAM/NAND pricing separately from bits; contracted volumes versus customer inventories; SCA floor renegotiation/default; the FY2027 sequential path; fab construction versus economically usable yields; grant collection/clawback; cash taxes; and incremental returns on the enlarged asset base. Earlier price reversal, persistent oversupply or weaker contract enforcement moves toward bear. Evidence of durable differentiated margins after supply expansion could justify bull. A demand forecast is not confirmed merely by customer capital-spending announcements.

8. Research audit and remaining gates

Latest release, annual filing, eight quarter pairs, investor deck, and readable Q3/Q4 prepared remarks were reviewed. No video/audio viewing is claimed. No full commercial transcript was retained. Source IDs, publication dates, URLs and verification statuses are in evidence-MU.html#sources; evidence-MU.html#facts separates reported facts, derived items and open data. The proposed scenarios are complete as research assumptions, but cash-tax settlement, customer refunds, grant contingencies, award overhang and valuation-date bridge prevent public per-share release. No app or production data was edited.

Broadcom forecast and valuation dossier

As of 2026-10-17. USD amounts unless stated. Provisional scenarios, with unresolved financing and equity-value gates.

What changes the base case

Latest quarterly revenue was $29.591bn, up 86% year over year; GAAP EBIT $15.955bn, a 53.92% margin. Latest TTM revenue/EBIT were $89.104bn/$42.814bn. AI is accelerating far faster than the old undifferentiated 35% growth assumption, but memory pass-through, customer concentration and financing support make a simple high-margin extrapolation incomplete.

September 2 issuer results cover FY2026 Q3 ended August 2. The 10-Q was accepted September 9 at 21:56:42 UTC and filed September 10. Latest actuals and contractual terms are separated from management outlooks below.

Business, mix and historical development

Quarterly semiconductors were $20.839bn, 70.4% of revenue; infrastructure software $8.752bn, 29.6%. AI semiconductors were $16.7bn, a subset of semiconductors and 56.4% of total revenue, up 221% year over year and 54% sequentially. The balance includes slower non-AI chips and VMware/other software, so applying AI growth to the entire company would overstate the forecast. Semiconductor/software revenue progressed from $12.515bn/$6.796bn in Q1 to $15.009bn/$7.178bn in Q2 and $20.839bn/$8.752bn in Q3. Q2 segments are derived from nine-month less Q1 and Q3 figures.

Annual revenue growth was 7.9% in FY2023, 44.0% in FY2024 and 23.9% in FY2025. FY2024 includes VMware acquisition effects and is not organic growth. GAAP EBIT margins were 45.2%, 26.1% and 39.9%; acquisition amortization and restructuring complicate comparisons. FY2025 revenue/EBIT were $63.887bn/$25.484bn. Annual financial and source history is in evidence-AVGO.html#facts.

Guidance, revisions and leadership context

Q4 FY2026 issuer guidance is approximately $34.8bn corporate revenue, $21.7bn AI revenue and 66% non-GAAP operating margin. Q4 ends November 1 and has not been reported at cutoff. The September 2 public call transcript raises FY2026 AI revenue from $56bn to $58bn and FY2027 from over $100bn to approximately $115bn, adding FY2028 $230bn. Those are AI-segment forecasts reported in a public secondary transcript, not independently issuer-document-verified official guidance. They are future and unscored, not consolidated revenue or binding customer cash obligations. Management said it did not intend to update the multi-year trajectory quarterly.

Management described supply secured against these plans but also depends on customer sites, land/power/shell and financing. Customer GW deployment plans are not booked revenue. Q4 capex outlook was $1.4bn, reflecting growing direct capacity investment. Memory pass-through reduces percentage gross margin; strong revenue growth can coexist with lower gross-margin percentage.

The March 20, 2024 issuer investor-day slides show multi-generation custom-accelerator strategy and an early $10bn-plus FY2024 AI outlook. A future million-accelerator cluster illustration is a scale vision, not corporate financial guidance. Hock Tan's June 5 Bloomberg Tech interview was read through a public transcription, with primary-host event metadata checked; no video was watched. His account of an early customer bet and competition with customer insourcing informs risk interpretation, not a numerical credibility score.

Earnings quality, cash investment and ROIC

Q3 non-GAAP operating income was $20.095bn versus GAAP $15.955bn; exclusions include $2.019bn SBC and $2.006bn acquisition intangible amortization. A 67.91% non-GAAP operating margin cannot be used as GAAP EBIT without a reconciliation. Segment profit also excludes corporate items.

Nine-month CFO was $32.950bn, capex $1.013bn, depreciation $484m and intangible/right-of-use amortization $6.047bn. SBC was $6.287bn. Receivables and inventory absorbed $8.797bn; payables provided $2.313bn. The existing historical D&A mapping is depreciation-only for Broadcom, an important model gap. ROU amortization also needs a consistent lease convention. Physical capex alone understates economic capital deployed through customer finance and purchase commitments. The latest filing also says most new software contracts no longer permit termination for convenience; additional license recognition contributed to Q3 growth. Distinguish recognition timing from recurring demand when forecasting VMware.

Reported book sales/capital ratios reflect $97.801bn goodwill and $26.325bn intangibles at August 2, not an organic factory efficiency measure. The FY2025 effective tax rate was negative because of discrete items, unsuitable as a normalized operating rate. A 20% normalized tax rate, 2x forward incremental sales/capital and 20% terminal ROIC are explicit judgments, not reported operating facts.

Obligations and asset bridge: unresolved

The evidence-AVGO.html#judgment register contains source, measurement date, conditionality and treatment for:

  • $59.419bn carrying debt, $23.975bn cash and the incomplete current lease reconciliation.
  • $126.821bn enforceable purchase commitments, including $52.674bn FY2027 and $72.952bn FY2028. The schedule excludes cancelable-without-penalty agreements and remaining terms of one year or less, so it is not total near-term procurement.
  • $3.941bn other contracts; $1.755bn uncertain-timing tax benefits/interest/penalties excluded from that schedule.
  • The customer-financing backstop: maximum $29bn undiscounted after all rack deployment. It covers a default-related difference between 85% of outstanding lease obligations and asset-disposal proceeds over five-year leases, with alternative remedies. Reported fair value was immaterial and no payment had occurred. Maximum contractual exposure is not expected loss or funded debt.
  • Up to $42bn conditional notes that the customer may issue TO Broadcom for customer lease obligations. None existed at August 2. This is potential investment/funding exposure, not Broadcom convertible debt. Reconcile its overlap with the backstop before modeling simultaneous losses.
  • 165m unvested RSUs, $18.221bn unrecognized SBC over 2.9 years, versus 4,773.629865m cover shares on August 28. Future compensation expense is not award fair value. Current holdings beyond cash remain unreconciled.

One distributor was 50% of quarterly revenue; the top five end customers approximately 55%. These overlap and cannot be added. The same concentration can damage operating revenue, receivables, financing recoveries and supplier obligations simultaneously. No unconditional $29bn/$42bn deduction or zero-claim assumption is appropriate.

Management capabilities and failure conditions

Observed strengths are conservative short-horizon revenue guidance, custom-silicon execution, operating leverage and historical cash conversion/debt repayment. Evidence is less mature for expanded customer financing. Hock Tan led throughout; Kirsten Spears was CFO through June 12, 2026, then Amie Thuener. Do not attribute the whole history to the new CFO. Product insourcing, site delays, customer funding, memory cost/mix, VMware renewal economics and contingent loss/recovery are the main invalidators. The dimension-specific evidence-AVGO.html#management preserves counterexamples.

Source limits and adoption gate

Primary releases, current/annual SEC filings and investor-day slides were reviewed. A readable issuer-hosted call transcript was not found, so public Quartr direct-speech transcriptions are labeled as secondary; dates and quarterly figures are corroborated with issuer sources. No video/audio was watched, no full commercial transcript stored and no paywall bypass used. No analyst consensus archive was collected. evidence-AVGO.html#sources lists gaps. These scenarios cannot become final valuation defaults until capital, lease, fiscal-period and contingent-credit bridges are completed. No app edits or price calibration were made.

TSMC (TSM): forecast and valuation dossier

As of 17 October 2026. Native TWD millions in JSON; narrative often uses TWD trillions. USD figures are explicitly labeled. Research assumptions, not a price target. Currency and ADS gates remain active.

Decision summary

TSMC's leading-node/advanced-packaging position and recent execution support strong near-term growth and longer persistence than a commodity-memory supplier. They do not justify compounding management's2024–2029 target for five fresh years from today. The preferred base starts with the TIFRS TTM revenue of TWD4.944817tr, models five explicit early years, and fades growth/returns across15 years. The base reaches46% EBIT margin,18% terminal ROIC and2% terminal growth, with capital intensity rising as growth matures.

TTM accounting, flow FX, valuation-date spot FX and the5ordinary-shares-per-ADS ratio must remain separate. No per-ADS output is released until current claims, share precision and date-consistent spot FX are reconciled.

TSMC is a dedicated foundry with one reportable foundry segment. Platform and technology mixes describe revenue drivers, not independently valued operating segments. Q3 revenue mix was HPC68%, smartphone21%, IoT4%, automotive4%, digital consumer1% and other2%. HPC is broader than AI accelerators. Wafer-revenue mix was2nm8%,3nm33%,5nm28%,7nm10%, older21%; 7nm-and-below represented79%. North American customers contributed79% of revenue. Q3 management report

Q3 revenue was TWD1.494243tr, EBIT TWD0.876445tr and parent net income TWD0.763064tr. TWD revenue grew50.9% while USD revenue grew41.2%, and12-inch-equivalent wafer shipments grew9.6% to4.476m. Thus mix, realized value per wafer and currency, not just units, drive growth. The FY2025 top-ten customers accounted for78% of revenue; the largest two represented19% and17%. 5. WACC, units and mechanical valuation audit

Native TWD flows use nominal TWD WACC: base10%, bull8.5%, bear13%. Construction begins with the verified October 16 USD10-year5.09% and judgmentERP4.5%, beta/debt spread/weights and risk allowances, then translates using assumed long-run USD inflation2.5% andTWD1.5%. These are scenario assumptions, not measured current TWD risk-free rates or observed beta/spreads. Exact inputs and common-market reference are in evidence-TSM.html#judgment. Currency-specific risk adjustment is not a substitute for a separate Taiwan continuity scenario.

Mechanics: base: operating EV 46.75 TWD tr, terminal PV 38.6%; bull: operating EV 105.45 TWD tr, terminal PV 51.7%; bear: operating EV 15.12 TWD tr, terminal PV 22.9%. These are native operating values before claims, precise stub timing and currency/share conversion. Terminal reinvestment = growth/ROIC; growth remains below WACC. A higher terminal return without evidence would reduce required investment and inflate value.

TheQ3 flow rate31.983 and9M31.744 translate income/flows. TheSeptember 30balance-sheet spot31.880 is neither theQ3average nor verified valuation-date spot. Once the bridge is complete, TWD equity per ordinary share is divided by independently verified valuation-date TWD/USD and multiplied by5 to obtainUSDper ADS. Dividing TWDenterprisevalue directly byADSshares, using flow FX for equity, or omitting the5x ratio are release-blocking errors.

Capitalization and maintenance policy

Reported R&D remains expensed; no synthetic research asset, amortization add-back or starting EBIT rewrite is used. A later capitalization choice must adjust both earnings and invested capital consistently. SBC remains expensed. Maintenance/technology-refresh capex is not separately disclosed: D&A is a consistency proxy, not a claim that accounting depreciation equals economic replacement. The later D&A audit is20% of sales. Base year15 implied capex is TWD4.323tr versus D&A3.616tr, retaining substantial replacement plus growth spending. Tool inflation, obsolescence and uncommenced leases can require more cash than this proxy; the downside does not assume immediate factory liquidation. Cash-flow capitalization/lease reconciliation remains a final implementation gate.

7. Management capabilities and counterevidence

C.C. Wei has been CEO sinceJune 2018 and chairman sinceJune 2024, following a co-CEO role fromNovember 2013. Wendell Huang has been CFO sinceSeptember 2019 andSVP sinceFebruary 2024. This tenure permits meaningful execution review, but does not isolate their contribution from customer architectures, ecosystem strength, currency and industry conditions. FY2025 20-F

  • Demand forecasting (medium-high short term, medium long term confidence): Strong recent quarterly execution and conservative ranges; multiyear demand remains a judgment. Evidence/outcome: Eight consecutive reported quarters meet or exceed original USD revenue range; five above, three within. Management checks customers and their customers and now reports checking data-center build-outs/power. Supports a strong near-term starting path, not automatic 25% growth from today. Counterevidence: Raising 2026 capex from $52-56bn to $60-64bn demonstrates forecast revision rather than perfect foresight. 2023 revenue declined in the historical record. Demand signals may overlap across customers; signed product plans are not end-user monetization.
  • Product delivery (high recent, medium forward confidence): Leading-node ramp has revenue and yield evidence; future A14 remains a roadmap. Evidence/outcome: N2 entered high-volume production Q4 2025 and accounts for 8% of Q3 2026 wafer revenue. 7nm-and-below is 79% of wafer revenue. Demonstrated ability to monetize leading nodes, enabling measured persistence in margin/returns. Counterevidence: A14 2027 risk/2028 volume-production objectives are not realized. Node mix and competitor yield improvements can change advantage quickly.
  • Capacity execution (medium-high confidence): Operational ramp competence is visible, with larger overseas execution burden ahead. Evidence/outcome: Arizona first fab high-volume production confirmed in Q4 2024. N2 now ramps across Hsinchu/Kaohsiung; capacity expected to more than double in 2027. Capacity delivers current shipments, but almost 20 fab projects make forward workload unusually large. Counterevidence: Overseas dilution increases as several fabs open. Tool availability, power/water, skills, labor and subsidies can delay economically usable output.
  • Cost control (medium-high confidence): Better utilization and productivity repeatedly beat margin guidance; FX and mix must be separated from skill. Evidence/outcome: Q3 2026 58.7% EBIT margin versus 56-58% guide; Q2 60.3% versus 56.5-58.5%. Q3 gross margin fell 1.3 points as N2 ramp diluted margins, as directionally anticipated. Justifies above-industry mature economics, with explicit fade for foreign-fab cost. Counterevidence: 2025Q3 favorable currency versus guide helped margins; not all beat is cost control. N2 and overseas costs can outlast productivity gains.
  • Capital allocation (medium-high historical, medium forecast confidence): Investment has supported profitable growth, but new capex is a demanding long-duration commitment. Evidence/outcome: FY2025 operating cash flow TWD2.275tr versus capex TWD1.272tr. Current balance sheet has substantial cash/investments; regular dividends. Model requires reinvestment and returns decay; no valuation premium solely for leadership reputation. Counterevidence: Higher construction/tool cost per wafer and foreign fab economics may depress future incremental returns. Cash/ROE is not ROIC; refundable customer receipts and NCI/leases affect claims. Taiwan continuity risk is outside management control.

Each domain has evidence, outcome, confidence, counterexamples and source IDs in evidence-TSM.html#management. No management reputation score or automatic valuation multiplier is used.

8. Risks, invalidators and research gates

Watch leading-node utilization versus added capacity; N2/A14 qualification and yields; CoWoS/packaging throughput; customer concentration; overseas fab cost and subsidies; supplier/tool/energy inflation; export restrictions; and power/water continuity. More wafer revenue per unit can reflect value creation but also creates exposure to high-end demand concentration. Multi-quarter revenue shortfalls, slower node qualification or foreign-margin dilution beyond the modeled path invalidate the base. Customer capex announcements and overlapping forecasts do not prove ultimate demand or monetization.

Taiwan geopolitical disruption, earthquakes and operational concentration deserve explicit stress scenarios. A few WACC points cannot faithfully encode total interruption or asset loss. The annual filing recorded earthquake-related losses in 2024/2025, demonstrating nonzero physical disruption risk; the proposed bear assumes continued operation. Annual risks and note37

Research covered current quarter, eight matched guidance quarters, annual/local filings and readable prepared/Q&A transcripts.
